title: popup.html hardcodes version 'v1.5.0', manifest.json is 1.7.0
description: Discovered during oculist-rnr.3 and confirmed by review. extension/popup.html:473 hardcodes 'v1.5.0' while extension/manifest.json is 1.7.0. Every user who opens the toolbar popup in the v1.7.0 build sees v1.5.0, and the string is legible in screenshots/05-vision-profiles.png, which is bound for the store listing. Shipping a v1.7.0 listing whose screenshot reads v1.5.0 invites reviewer suspicion that the package does not match the listing. Fix the SOURCE of the recurrence, not just the digits. Hardcoding '1.7.0' recreates this bug at the next release. Steps: 1. In extension/popup.js, set the version text at runtime from chrome.runtime.getManifest().version rather than leaving it in markup. Give the span a stable id or reuse an existing selector; keep the leading 'v' prefix so the rendered string stays 'v1.7.0'. 2. In extension/popup.html:473, leave the span empty (or with a neutral placeholder) so no version literal remains in markup. Verify no other file hardcodes a version string: grep -rn 'v1\.[0-9]' extension/ and fix any other stale literal found the same way. 3. Re-run the capture so the store screenshots show the correct version: node scripts/screenshots.js 4. Confirm screenshots/05-vision-profiles.png now reads v1.7.0, and that all 5 PNGs remain exactly 1280x800. Edge cases: - chrome.runtime.getManifest() is synchronous and available in popup context; do NOT wrap it in an async storage call. - If the popup renders before the DOM node exists, set the text after DOMContentLoaded or wherever popup.js already does its initial render. Follow the file's existing initialisation pattern. - Do NOT bump any version number anywhere. manifest.json is already correct at 1.7.0. - If the recapture changes other screenshots incidentally, that is fine, but all 5 must remain 1280x800 and 02-multi-term-list.png must still show 3 chips with the active/dim distinction. Done-criteria: - No version literal remains in extension/popup.html or any other extension source; grep -rn 'v1\.[0-9]' extension/ returns nothing stale. - The popup renders 'v1.7.0', sourced from the manifest. - screenshots/05-vision-profiles.png visibly reads v1.7.0. - All 5 screenshots verified 1280x800. - npm test passes at exactly 212 tests, 212 pass, 0 fail.

title: Four new beacon effects (registry 9 to 13)
description:
Add Speed Lines, Chrono Tunnel, Light Cycle and Cyber-Vision to effectsRegistry, taking it from 9 effects to 13. Visual design is APPROVED and mocked up live at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2ecca129-a2f3-478d-8a3c-d84ad87f72f5 - this epic is implementation, not design exploration. Open the mockup before starting any effect bead; it is the spec.

TWO DECISIONS ALREADY MADE BY THE OPERATOR, do not revisit:
1. Light Cycle ships ALONGSIDE the existing trail effect. animateTrail is NOT removed. The two overlap visibly (both trace an L-path to the match) and that is accepted for now; a follow-up bead can revisit once both are live.
2. Chrono Tunnel's hue RIDES getEffectiveColors().beacon with a bounded sweep, NOT the full 360-degree spectrum of the mockup. Oculist is a vision-accessibility product with a user-set beacon colour and a motionSensitivity setting; full-spectrum cycling would ignore both.

SHARED CONTRACTS every effect must follow, verified in extension/content.js:
- Signature animateX(rect); bail immediately on !rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0.
- Container div, className 'oc-beacon', position:absolute at DOCUMENT coords (rect.left + window.scrollX, rect.top + window.scrollY), pointer-events:none, z-index 2147483640, appended to document.documentElement NOT body. See drawStaticActiveBorder (content.js:2038) and animateElectronCloud (content.js:1895) for the working pattern.
- Colour from getEffectiveColors().beacon. Size from getBeaconScale(). EVERY duration wrapped in getBeaconDuration(base) so the animationSpeed setting works.
- Canvas effects MUST set container.__rafId = animFrameId on every frame, or cancelBeacons() (content.js:818-825) cannot cancel them and beacons leak across searches.
- Self-removal via setTimeout(function(){ container.remove(); }, total).
- Lite Mode: settings.performanceMode scales counts and geometry DOWN inside the effect function.
- Reduced motion is handled CENTRALLY by animate() (content.js:2599-2623), which short-circuits to animateReducedMotion() BEFORE dispatching to the registry. Individual effects must NOT add their own reduced-motion branch.
- i18n label near content.js:577-585; registry entry near content.js:682-690.
- Plain var/function inside the IIFE. No ES modules, no new dependencies.

TESTING: node --test plus Playwright, run as OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3 npm test (160 tests at epic start; plain npm test flakes on the dev box, see oculist-li8). Budgets derive from test/helpers/wait.js, never hardcoded. Test hooks live under window.__ocTest. Model on test/dispersion_bloom.test.js and test/trail_effect.test.js. Every effect needs coverage that FAILS against a plausible wrong implementation, covers its Lite Mode path, and asserts no .oc-beacon element leaks.

title: Shipped v1.5.0: find-in-page self-matches Oculist's own overlay text
description:
CONFIRMED SHIPPED DEFECT in released v1.6.0. Already fixed on epic/oculist-l6m by
oculist-l6m.4; this bead exists so the fix is tracked and a patch release can be considered
rather than the fix being buried in a feature commit.

Cause: buildPageIndex()'s traverse() recursed into any child.shadowRoot with no exclusion.
#oc-wrap is attachShadow({mode:'open'}) and appended to document.body, so traverse
(document.body) walked Oculist's own overlay text into the searchable flat text.

Repro on released v1.6.0, on a page containing zero occurrences of the word "of":
1. Ctrl+F, search "cat" -> overlay shows "1 of 3"
2. Search "of" -> overlay shows "1 of 1"
The match does not exist on the page. It is the overlay's own count text.

Same class of failure for i18n.noMatch ("no match") and for every settings-panel label
while the gear panel is open.

Fix applied in .4: added `child !== wrap` to the element-skip guard in traverse().
Verified by reverting only that guard in a copied tree and driving both builds through
Playwright.

Done: decide whether this warrants a v1.6.1 patch release ahead of the v1.7.0 feature
merge, and record the decision here.
notes:
CORRECTION: this bead originally said 'shipped v1.6.0'. The oculist-l6m.10 review established that 1.6.0 NEVER SHIPPED (only v1.5.0 is tagged, dist/ holds no 1.6.0 artifact, and commit 26d10f6 sets the convention that a dated CHANGELOG heading means released). The affected released version is therefore v1.5.0, the current Chrome Web Store build. The hotfix decision is whether to patch v1.5.0 ahead of the v1.7.0 feature merge, or let v1.7.0 carry the fix.
SKIPPED by the /goal follow-up run, deliberately and not as an oversight. This bead's content is a decision reserved to the human (patch v1.5.0 ahead of the v1.7.0 merge, or let v1.7.0 carry the fix). An implementer dispatched at it would be inventing the answer. Left open and unclaimed.

title: Working-list session storage plumbing (oc-worklist)
description:
Give the content script read/write access to a session-scoped working list.

Steps:
1. repo/extension/background.js: at service-worker startup call
   chrome.storage.session.setAccessLevel({accessLevel: 'TRUSTED_AND_UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS'}).
   Wrap in try/catch; older Chrome without setAccessLevel must not break the worker.
2. repo/extension/content.js: add loadWorkList() and saveWorkList(list) around
   chrome.storage.session key 'oc-worklist', shape {terms: string[], activeIndex: number}.
3. Both helpers check chrome.runtime.lastError. A failed read resolves to
   {terms: [], activeIndex: -1} so the overlay degrades to today's single-term behaviour
   with no error shown to the user.
4. Do NOT touch 'oc-settings', SETTINGS_KEYS, or the pendingSelfWrites echo-suppression.

Edge cases: storage.session may be undefined in a content script if step 1 failed; guard
for it. Reads must never throw into the overlay mount path.

Done: a test asserts a saved working list round-trips, and that a rejected/failed read
yields the empty default rather than throwing.

title: Multi-term search lists (v1.7.0)
description:
Let the user hold a list of search terms, run them against the current page, and carry
the list to the next page. One term is active at a time with the full existing beacon
treatment; the rest stay dim-highlighted. Named lists persist in sync storage.

Approved design: ../artifacts/plans/v1.7.0-2026-08-25-multi-term-lists-design.md
(from repo root: /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/plans/v1.7.0-2026-08-25-multi-term-lists-design.md)

Shape of the change:
- performSearch() splits into buildPageIndex() + findRanges(); performListSearch() runs
  the index once and findRanges per term.
- searchRanges stays the active term's ranges, so findNext/highlightActiveRange/beacons/
  viewport markers need no changes.
- Three CSS.highlights registries with explicit priorities: dim(0) < match(1) < active(2).
- Working list in chrome.storage.session (oc-worklist); saved lists in chrome.storage.sync
  one key per list (oc-list-<id>).
- No new manifest permissions.

Non-goals: merged cross-term navigation, auto-running a list on page load, list management
in the popup.

title: Stop DOM-mutation rescan from scrolling the viewport back to the active match
description: Oculist's MutationObserver-driven rescan called highlightActiveRange(false), which ran element.scrollIntoView(...) and yanked the viewport back to the active match whenever the page mutated (lazy-load, infinite scroll) while the user was scrolling elsewhere. Fix: added skipScroll parameter to highlightActiveRange, passed true from rescanAfterMutation, and gated the scroll branch on !skipScroll. Interactive navigation (typing search, prev/next, replay) is unaffected.

Defect 2: claims the extension 'runs fine on strict Content Security Policy sites like GitHub'. False. extension/background.js:65 ships DEFAULT_DISABLED_SITES = ['github.com']; CHANGELOG 1.5.0 and PRIVACY.md both state Ctrl+F falls through to native find on GitHub out of the box.

The v1.7.0 doc was corrected under oculist-rnr.5. This bead covers the two remaining exposures:

2. HUMAN ACTION: check whether the live Chrome Web Store listing description currently contains either claim. If it does, it is a false statement on a public listing contradicting the linked privacy policy, and should be corrected at the same time the v1.7.0 update is submitted.

Item 2 requires dashboard access and is not actionable by an agent.

title: Refresh store screenshots to 5, covering the v1.7.0 multi-term feature
description:
The Chrome Web Store accepts a MAXIMUM of 5 screenshots at 1280x800 or 640x400. screenshots/ currently holds SIX 1280x800 PNGs captured 2026-07-30, all predating v1.7.0. None show multi-term search lists, which is v1.7.0's headline feature, and none show the three new effects.

Existing files: 01-find-bar, 02-matches, 03-beacon-warp, 04-settings, 05-beacon-spotlight, 06-vision-profiles.

Steps:
1. Read scripts/screenshots.js to learn how the existing captures are driven (Playwright, target page, which UI state each shot sets up). Reuse that harness — do NOT hand-roll a new capture script.
2. Decide a final set of exactly 5, ordered for conversion per the store guidance: (1) core interaction on a real page, (2) the v1.7.0 multi-term list in action with several terms and the dim/active treatment visible, (3) effect variety, (4) settings/vision profiles, (5) popup or toolbar UI. Reuse existing shots where they still represent shipped 1.7.0 UI; recapture only what is stale or missing.
3. Add or adjust capture steps in scripts/screenshots.js so the multi-term list shot is reproducible, not a one-off manual capture.
4. Run the capture. Every output PNG must be exactly 1280x800. Verify with: sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight screenshots/*.png
5. Remove or move aside the sixth file so screenshots/ holds exactly 5 store-bound PNGs. Prefer renaming the surplus into screenshots/unused/ over deleting it — do NOT rm any capture that the script cannot regenerate.
6. Renumber the final set 01..05 so filename order equals store display order.

Edge cases:
- If Playwright cannot launch in this environment, STOP and report it. Do NOT fabricate screenshots, do NOT hand-edit PNGs, and do NOT claim a capture succeeded that did not run.
- If an existing shot already shows shipped 1.7.0 UI correctly, keep the file byte-identical rather than recapturing for the sake of it.

Done-criteria:
- screenshots/ contains exactly 5 store-bound PNGs, each verified 1280x800.
- One of them visibly demonstrates a multi-term list with more than one term highlighted.
- scripts/screenshots.js reproduces the full set in one run.
- npm test passes.

title: Speed Lines: central highlight line at the match's vertical position
description: Add a horizontal highlight line to animateSpeedLines, sort of like the anime laser's beam: a thin line at the match's vertical center (the effect's matchY anchor, already exposed via __ocTest.lastSpeedLinesAnchor), spanning the effect's width, visible for the effect's full duration. Colour from getEffectiveColors().beacon; thickness fixed with the container-level scale handling sizing (match how Speed Lines scales today); every duration through getBeaconDuration; Lite Mode may simplify (thinner/no glow) but the line itself should remain since it IS the accessibility aid; reduced motion stays central in animate(), no per-effect branch. Canvas vs DOM: implement inside the existing Speed Lines rendering approach (it is canvas - draw the line each frame at lane centre) rather than bolting on a separate DOM element, unless the implementer finds the DOM route clearly simpler. TEST: extend test/speed_lines.test.js - assert the line exists at the anchor's matchY (use the dvt.7 anchor helper pattern for an independent source of truth: the line's y must equal the target rect's centre mapped into container coords), that it persists mid-effect, and that a mutation offsetting the line's y breaks the test. DONE: line renders at the match's vertical centre for the effect duration, verified against the target rect independently; full suite green.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Landed: 2px core line at hexToRgba(beacon, 0.6) drawn every frame at the shared offsetY anchor, full canvas width, inside the existing lighter-composite block; 8px glow pass gated off in Lite Mode (core stays - it is the accessibility locator). Three tests: position graded against elementCenterInContainer (independent DOM truth), full-duration persistence via lockstep draw/frame counters read atomically, Lite Mode presence. Reviewer notes for the record: occlusion judged acceptable (the flare already draws a white 2px core through the word, and anime laser's 8px opacity-1 beam is far stronger precedent); tests grade the highlightY hook rather than rasterized pixels - both hook and fillRect read the same local, but a fillRect-only mutation would survive; acceptable proxy consistent with the file's anchor-test pattern.

title: Remove the Light Cycle effect (registry 13 to 12)
description: Operator decision 2026-08-28, superseding the oculist-dvt-era note that Light Cycle ships alongside Trail: remove Light Cycle entirely. Scope: (1) effectsRegistry entry 'lightcycle' and its i18n label; (2) animateLightCycle and everything only it uses (MIN_SEG_SEP guard, .oc-lightcycle-box CSS if any, data-oc-lc-index only if unused elsewhere); (3) delete test/light_cycle.test.js; remove the lightcycle case from test/waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js and the Light Cycle case from test/box_sizing_defense.test.js (keep those files' other coverage intact); (4) the four prose enumerations drop to 12: extension/welcome.html prose ('Choose from 13 effects') and mockup option list, docs/index.html intro and Showing lines - test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js enforces all four, so run it to find every stale site; (5) any settings-panel or docs references. DONE: no lightcycle/LightCycle/light-cycle identifier or label remains outside git history; effect_enumeration_sync passes at 12; full suite green with no orphaned tests.

title: Cyber-Vision effect (DOM/CSS targeting HUD)
description:
SECOND DOM effect. Follows the DOM/WAAPI pattern established by the Light Cycle bead - read that implementation and its tests first.

INPUT: the approved mockup at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2ecca129-a2f3-478d-8a3c-d84ad87f72f5 (fourth bench, key 'cybervision').

OUTPUT: animateCyberVision(rect) in extension/content.js, i18n label effectCyberVision: 'Cyber-Vision', and a registry entry cybervision. NO CANVAS - this is DOM plus CSS only.

DESIGN, four layers composited over the viewport:
1. A tint wash and a scanline overlay (repeating-linear-gradient, roughly 1px line every 4px) that fade in and out across the whole effect.
2. A bright bar sweeping the full viewport height once, with a hard bright edge on its leading side.
3. Thermal false-colour blocks resolving over the match: a grid roughly 3 rows deep by (match width / 9) columns, each block randomly assigned one of four heat colours, staggered in by column so they appear to resolve left to right.
4. Targeting brackets - four corner elements, each built from a div with two borders removed - that snap inward onto the match from outside, hold, then fade. Alongside them a monospace readout.

READOUT: the mockup shows placeholder text. Evaluate whether it should instead carry the REAL match index and count, the way drawActiveMatchMagnifier already absorbs the counter (see content.js:2565-2570, where the magnifier suppresses the count element when it draws). This is an OPTION to assess, not a requirement - if wiring it means duplicating counter logic or fighting the magnifier for the same job, report that and ship static-but-honest text instead. Say which you chose and why.

ACCESSIBILITY: the readout is decorative chrome, not content. It must not be announced by screen readers and must not collide with the existing chip and counter accessible names. Mark it aria-hidden.

TIMING: about 1000ms total, wrapped in getBeaconDuration(). Sweep about 620ms, brackets snapping at roughly 440ms.

LITE MODE: settings.performanceMode drops the thermal grid and the scanline overlay, keeping only the sweep and the brackets.

DONE:
- Selecting Cyber-Vision fires the effect on a match.
- A test asserts the brackets land on the match: all four corner elements sit within a few px of the match rect's corners. It FAILS if they are mispositioned.
- A test asserts the thermal blocks stagger rather than appearing together.
- A test asserts Lite Mode renders no thermal blocks and no scanline overlay.
- A test asserts the readout is aria-hidden and does not appear in the accessibility tree (test/helpers/accessible_name.js has a computed-name helper).
- A test asserts no .oc-beacon element survives after completion.

title: Light Cycle effect (DOM, persistent light wall)
description:
FIRST of the two DOM effects. Establishes the DOM/WAAPI pattern that Cyber-Vision then follows.

INPUT: the approved mockup at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2ecca129-a2f3-478d-8a3c-d84ad87f72f5 (third bench, key 'lightcycle').

OUTPUT: animateLightCycle(rect) in extension/content.js, i18n label effectLightCycle: 'Light Cycle', and a registry entry lightcycle.

MODEL IT ON animateTrail (content.js:1499), which already traces an L-shaped path to a match using the Web Animations API. This is the closest existing code; follow its structure rather than starting fresh.

DESIGN: a cycle head runs in toward the match on RIGHT ANGLES ONLY - no curves, no diagonals, that constraint is the whole aesthetic. Behind it, a solid glowing wall grows segment by segment: each segment is a div scaled from 0 to 1 along its own axis (scaleX for horizontal runs, scaleY for vertical), with transformOrigin set to the end the cycle entered from. The head is a small bright marker riding the segment boundary. On arrival the wall HOLDS, a box outline snaps around the match, and then the wall de-rezzes from the TAIL forward - segments fade in the order they were drawn, not all at once.

The persistence is the point: every other beacon is a flash, this one briefly leaves a path back to the match.

NOTE: this ships alongside the existing trail effect, which is NOT removed. The operator decided this. Do not delete or modify animateTrail.

TIMING: about 900ms for the run-in (roughly 300ms per segment across 3 segments), then a 400ms de-rez. All wrapped in getBeaconDuration().

LITE MODE: settings.performanceMode drops to a single straight segment plus the box outline, and skips the staggered de-rez.

DONE:
- Selecting Light Cycle fires the effect on a match.
- A test asserts the path is right-angled: every wall segment is either purely horizontal or purely vertical, no diagonals. It FAILS if a segment is given both a width and a height greater than a few pixels.
- A test asserts the segments de-rez in tail-first order, not simultaneously.
- A test asserts Lite Mode renders a single segment.
- A test asserts no .oc-beacon element survives after completion.
- animateTrail and test/trail_effect.test.js are untouched.

title: Chrono Tunnel effect (canvas, beacon-hued rings)
description:
SECOND canvas effect. Follows the canvas pattern established by the Speed Lines bead - read that implementation and its tests first, and reuse whatever it established rather than inventing a parallel approach.

INPUT: the approved mockup at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2ecca129-a2f3-478d-8a3c-d84ad87f72f5 (second bench, key 'chrono').

OUTPUT: animateChronoTunnel(rect) in extension/content.js, i18n label effectChronoTunnel: 'Chrono Tunnel', and a registry entry chrono.

DESIGN: a kaleidoscopic tunnel. Roughly 26 rotating polygons (about 7 sides each) receding from the match, scaled on an exponential radius curve so they appear to rush outward past the viewer. Additive blending. Each ring's radius wobbles as a function of angle, which is what produces the slit-scan smear - that wobble is the signature of the effect, not decoration. A soft core glow sits at the match. Rings fade as they approach the edge.

COLOUR - THE OPERATOR DECIDED THIS, DO NOT IMPLEMENT THE MOCKUP'S VERSION: the mockup cycles the full 360-degree spectrum. Ship instead a hue that RIDES the user's beacon colour: derive a base hue from getEffectiveColors().beacon, then sweep a BOUNDED range around it (about plus or minus 60 degrees across depth and time). Rationale: Oculist is a vision-accessibility product; a full-spectrum cycle ignores both the user's chosen beacon colour and the motionSensitivity setting, and would be the only effect in the registry that does. You will need a hex-to-hue conversion; check whether the file already has one (hslToHex exists near the dispersion effect) before adding its inverse.

TIMING: about 1100ms, wrapped in getBeaconDuration(). Envelope: ramp in over roughly the first 18 percent, hold, ramp out over the last 28 percent.

LITE MODE: settings.performanceMode collapses to a SINGLE hue (no sweep at all) and cuts the ring count hard (target roughly 8). This is the loudest of the four effects; Lite Mode must be genuinely calm.

DONE:
- Selecting Chrono Tunnel fires the effect on a match.
- A test proves the hue tracks the beacon colour: set two different beacon colours and assert the rendered ring hues differ correspondingly. The test FAILS if the implementation reverts to a fixed spectrum.
- A test asserts the sweep stays bounded - no rendered hue strays outside roughly plus or minus 60 degrees of the beacon hue.
- A test asserts Lite Mode uses a single hue and fewer rings.
- A test asserts no .oc-beacon element leaks, and container.__rafId is set every frame.

title: Speed Lines effect (canvas, horizontal streaks)
description:
FIRST of the two canvas effects. Establishes the canvas pattern that Chrono Tunnel then follows.

INPUT: the approved mockup at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2ecca129-a2f3-478d-8a3c-d84ad87f72f5 (first bench, key 'speedlines'). Read its live source for reference geometry.

OUTPUT: animateSpeedLines(rect) in extension/content.js, an i18n label effectSpeedLines: 'Speed Lines' near content.js:577-585, and a registry entry speedlines near content.js:682-690.

DESIGN: horizontal light streaks blasting outward from the match toward both edges. Roughly 74 gradient-filled rects. Additive blending (globalCompositeOperation 'lighter'). Three brightness tiers: hairline deep-hue lines, mid-weight lines, and thick bars carrying a white-hot core. Each streak is drawn with a linear gradient along its length so the trailing end tapers to transparent - that taper IS the motion blur, do not use a solid fill. Streak density is weighted toward the match's own line and thins toward the top and bottom of the viewport. A radial flare blooms at the match itself.

CRITICAL, this is the difference between a beacon and a nuisance: streaks crossing the match's own text band must be attenuated to roughly 12 percent alpha, creating a clear lane so the word stays readable. A find-in-page beacon must never obscure the thing it is pointing at. A reviewer will check this specifically.

COLOUR: the entire field is one hue parameter plus white cores, so it rides getEffectiveColors().beacon directly. Unlike Chrono Tunnel this needs no special handling - just derive the hue from the beacon colour.

TIMING: about 760ms total, wrapped in getBeaconDuration(). Fast attack (roughly the first 12 percent) then a long decay, so it reads as one impulse rather than a wash.

LITE MODE: settings.performanceMode cuts the streak count hard (target roughly 20) and drops the tier-2 bloom halos. Keep the clear lane and the flare.

DONE:
- Selecting Speed Lines in the settings panel fires the effect on a match.
- A test asserts the clear lane exists: streaks over the match band are measurably dimmer than streaks elsewhere, and the test FAILS if the attenuation is removed.
- A test asserts Lite Mode draws materially fewer streaks than full mode.
- A test asserts no .oc-beacon element survives after the effect finishes.
- container.__rafId is set every frame; cancelBeacons() demonstrably stops it mid-flight.

title: Dim treatment's colour is invisible on light pages at full opacity, so no contrast gate can rescue it
description: Found during oculist-l6m.17 review, with independently derived measurements. The dim treatment (both branches) is painted in the profile's matchColor, which on a white page is 1.164:1 for #fef08a (none, low-vision, deuteranopia, protanopia, warm), 1.427:1 for #ffcbd1 (tritanopia), and 1.040:1 for a pale custom colour like #fffbe6. All far below the 3:1 WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 non-text minimum, at FULL opacity - so this is not an alpha problem and no gate can fix it. At the current 0.35 dim alpha the per-profile ceiling across every possible grayscale background is 2.939:1 (#fef08a), 2.617:1 (#ffcbd1), 2.085:1 (#f59e0b fallback), meaning the alpha-wash branch is unreachable for every built-in profile on every background; it survives only for custom colours. FIX DIRECTION: derive the dim treatment's colour rather than inheriting matchColor - darken or lighten matchColor toward the background's opposite until the rendered treatment measures at least 3:1, then apply the existing wash-vs-underline choice. Done: the dim treatment as RENDERED (not merely the branch selected) measures at least 3:1 against the page background for every built-in profile including tritanopia, on both light and dark pages, verified by measured contrast. Depends on the decision taken for oculist-l6m.17.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: BETTER FIX DIRECTION, verified in Chromium: use the host page's own text colour via currentColor, instead of deriving a colour from matchColor. Probe result: currentColor inside ::highlight() resolves PER ELEMENT to that element's own text colour. A single ::highlight(oculist-dim-match) rule with text-decoration-color: currentColor rendered a #111 underline on a dark-text paragraph and a #eee underline on a light-text paragraph in the same registry, each pixel-identical to the corresponding fixed-colour render and different from a red control. Why this beats colour derivation: the page's text colour is already legible against the page's own background, or the page would be unreadable, so the dim mark inherits that guarantee rather than computing one. It needs no contrast math for the underline branch, and it removes the need for getPageBackgroundRgb() on that path entirely, which also fixes that function's stated limitation (it reads one page-level background and measures wrongly when text sits on a differently-coloured container, e.g. a dark card on a light page). Dark mode works with no branch. LIMITS: (1) Only the underline branch. A wash in currentColor would paint dark over dark text, so the wash still needs matchColor; since the l6m.17 review established the wash is unreachable for every built-in profile, the coherent shape is underline-in-currentColor for built-in profiles with the wash surviving only for custom colours that measure at or above 3:1. (2) The dim tier loses its palette hue, so match/active/dim hue separation no longer holds for dim; de-emphasis and identity come from the form (dotted, 2px) rather than colour. This is a design decision for the human, not a technical blocker. (3) color: transparent text (visually-hidden text, some icon-font techniques) yields a transparent underline; needs a fallback to a measured colour. Probe script: scratchpad/probe2.js from the 2026-08-26 /goal run.

title: keydownHandler's capture-phase Enter handling swallows native Enter-activation for settings/lists panel buttons
description: content.js's window-level keydown listener (capture:true) treats any Enter keypress while wrapRoot.activeElement is truthy as 'commit the find chip' and calls e.preventDefault() unconditionally, EXCEPT when focus is inside listsPanel (which has an explicit early-return guard). Settings panel buttons (theme/position/site-toggle/reset/etc, all real <button> elements) have no equivalent guard, so a keyboard user who tabs to one of those buttons and presses Enter never gets the native button click — the keydown's preventDefault() (running in capture phase, before the button's own default action) suppresses it, and instead the find-bar's chip-commit logic runs. Space still works (native click fires on keyup, untouched by this handler) so the panel is not totally unusable by keyboard, but Enter silently does the wrong thing. Discovered while writing the oculist-l6m.38 regression test (test/settings_panel_rebuild_focus.test.js), which had to use Space instead of Enter to activate a theme toggle button for that reason. Fix: mirror the listsPanel early-return guard for settingsPanel in keydownHandler's Enter branch.

title: Touching the magnifier silently drops the active vision profile
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.39 review. Contradicts that bead's own intent.

.39 deliberately kept visionSettings.magnifier out of every vision-profile PRESETS object so a
profile switch never clobbers an explicit choice. The spread-merge in popup.js:170-174 and
welcome.js:654,667 does honour that.

But popup.js:238-240 forces visionProfile = 'custom' whenever ANY vision setting is touched,
magnifier included. So flipping a toggle that no profile governs still drops the user's named
profile and unlocks the effect and colour sections. The user picks Low Vision, turns the
magnifier on, and their profile silently becomes Custom for no reason.

Done: toggling a setting that belongs to no preset leaves visionProfile alone; a test picks a
named profile, toggles the magnifier, and asserts the profile survives.

title: onChanged listener crashes in applyWrapPosition() when a settings change lands while the overlay is closed (wrap is null)
description: In extension/content.js's chrome.storage.onChanged listener (registered inside boot(), around the 'else' branch that calls injectHighlightStyles()/applyWrapPosition()/updateViewportMarkers()), applyWrapPosition() is called unconditionally whenever a relevant settings key changes and disabledSites does not include the current hostname. applyWrapPosition() assumes wrap is a live element ('wrap.style.cssText = ...'), but wrap is undefined/null whenever the find overlay is currently closed (__ocDestroy() resets it to null). Repro: open the overlay, close it (Escape/__ocDestroy), then have any other context (popup, another tab, or a direct chrome.storage.sync.set) write a settings change while it is closed -- content.js's onChanged handler throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading style)' inside applyWrapPosition(), visible in the console as 'Error in event handler'. Observed while writing test/active_match_magnifier.test.js's Playwright coverage for oculist-l6m.39 (magnifier overlay), where settings were seeded directly via chrome.storage.sync.set. Fix: guard the onChanged listener's else branch (or applyWrapPosition/updateViewportMarkers themselves) on 'if (wrap)' before touching wrap-dependent DOM, mirroring the existing 'if (settingsPanel)' guard already in that same branch.

title: Magnifier overlay: show the matched word enlarged beside the match
description:
Ships in 1.7.0 (not yet released), so the 1.7.0 CHANGELOG entry must gain a line for it.

WHY: with multi-term lists, several different terms are highlighted at once (active term bright,
inactive terms dim). A magnified render of the word you are actually on tells you which term the
beacon is pointing at, at a glance, without reading the surrounding text.

DESIGN (settled with the human, do not re-litigate):

1. COMPANION OVERLAY, NOT AN EFFECT. Add drawActiveMatchMagnifier(rect), called from
   drawActiveOverlays() at the point drawActiveMatchLabel(rect) is called today. It is NOT an
   eighth entry in effectsRegistry: it must compose with whichever effect is selected, and the
   registry's run(rect) contract has no access to the matched text.

2. ABSORBS THE COUNTER. When the magnifier is enabled, drawActiveMatchLabel is SKIPPED and the
   magnifier renders the counter itself: the word large, with "3 of 47" small and dim beneath it.
   Both currently want the same space above the match, so they must never both draw.
   Single node #oc-active-match-magnifier, class oc-beacon. Reuse drawActiveMatchLabel's dark
   pill, beacon-coloured border and viewport clamping so it reads as the same family.

3. SHOWS THE REAL PAGE TEXT, not the typed term. Use searchRanges[activeIndex].toString().
   Search is case-insensitive and accent-folded, so a search for "peanut" may match "Peanuts" or
   "PEANUT" on the page; showing the actual text is more informative and is the point of
   "magnify". Collapse internal whitespace (a match can span text nodes and line breaks).
   Truncate past ~24 characters with an ellipsis, since terms can be up to 100 chars.

4. SIZE IS RELATIVE TO THE PAGE. Derive font-size from the MATCH's own computed font-size x 2.5,
   clamped to roughly 16-48px. Deliberately do NOT use getBeaconScale(): bead oculist-l6m.11
   records that chip sizing already wrongly rides that beacon knob, and this must not repeat it.

5. MOTION: zoom-lift. Web Animations API, matching the existing effects' .animate() +
   anim.finished pattern. Three beats: render at the match's position at page font size with
   opacity 0; scale up and rise about 40px; the connector to the match fades in last. Duration
   via getBeaconDuration() so the speed setting applies.

6. MOTION SENSITIVITY IS NOT OPTIONAL. Gate on effectiveMotion(): 'reduced' fades in at final
   size and position with no scale and no lift; 'off' draws it statically with no animation at
   all. This is a vision-accessibility product; the magnifier must not be the one overlay that
   ignores those settings.

7. SETTING: new visionSettings.magnifier boolean, DEFAULT OFF, placed next to Text labels in the
   settings panel. visionSettings is already a persisted key, so SETTINGS_KEYS does not change.
   Deliberately NOT auto-gated on "2 or more terms in the working list": an overlay that appears
   and disappears with list length is surprising, and the magnifier is genuinely useful for a
   single term on a page with tiny text.

8. ACCESSIBILITY: the card is aria-hidden="true". The word is already page content, and
   oculist-l6m.16 just made chip counts announced; announcing a magnified duplicate would be
   noise on top of noise.

EDGE CASES:
- Match near the viewport top: flip the card below the match rather than clamping it on top of
  the match. Reuse the existing label's maxLeft/maxTop clamping for the horizontal case.
- Resize: repositionActiveOverlays() already redraws overlays from a stored rect. The magnifier
  must join that path or it strands in old document coordinates.
- Teardown: __ocDestroy and the beacon sweep must remove #oc-active-match-magnifier. It is
  oc-beacon classed, so verify the existing sweep catches it rather than assuming.
- A match whose range yields an empty or whitespace-only string must not render an empty card.
- Zero matches: nothing to magnify, draw nothing.

DONE:
- The magnified card shows the real matched text with its original casing.
- The counter is absorbed; drawActiveMatchLabel never double-draws with it.
- reduced and off motion settings produce no scale or lift.
- The card is aria-hidden.
- It flips below the match near the viewport top, repositions on resize, and is removed on teardown.
- CHANGELOG.md's existing 1.7.0 "Added" section gains a line describing the magnifier.
- npm test passes with new Playwright coverage for each of the above.

title: Settings panel rebuilds drop focus out of the shadow root
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.27 review, verified with a live CDP probe. Pre-existing, but it directly
undercuts .27's "focus lives in the panel" contract.

content.js:3478, :3527, :3574 and :5164-5167 remove and rebuild settingsPanel in place (on a
theme change, a colour pick, and similar) without restoring focus. After a theme change the probe
shows shadowRoot.activeElement === null and document.activeElement === BODY.

A keyboard user changing any setting is silently ejected from the panel to the document body and
has to tab back in from scratch.

Done: an in-place rebuild restores focus to the equivalent control, or at minimum to the panel
container; a test changes a setting by keyboard and asserts focus is still inside the panel.

title: Escape destroys the whole overlay when the settings dialog is open
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.27 review, verified with a live CDP probe.

content.js:3197-3204: Escape with listsPanel open closes just that panel, but Escape with
settingsPanel open destroys the ENTIRE overlay (#oc-wrap gone, focus dropped to body).

This was deliberately scoped out in .9, when only listsPanel carried role="dialog". Bead .27
added role="dialog" to settingsPanel too, which creates the APG expectation that Escape
dismisses the dialog rather than the whole UI. The two now-identically-roled dialogs behave
differently for the same key.

No test covers settings + Escape.

Done: Escape closes the settings panel and returns focus to gearBtn; a second Escape closes the
overlay, matching the lists panel; tests cover both dialogs.

title: removeChipAt never rescans, leaving count and highlights disagreeing
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.19 review. Same symptom class as .19's CASE 2, different root cause,
and verified identical before and after .19 (so .19 neither caused nor fixed it).

removeChipAt (content.js:2739-2755) never rescans and never clears searchRanges or the
oculist-match registry.

Repro: with one chip whose term has 3 matches, press Backspace in an empty input to remove it.
The UI shows "0 of 3" with nav ENABLED and 3 highlights still lit on the page. Pressing Enter
then blanks the count while the 3 highlights stay lit.

Done: removing a chip leaves the count, the nav enabled-state, and the highlights in agreement;
a test covers backspace-removal of the only chip and of the active chip among several.

title: Test suite is wall-clock dependent: 106 fixed sleeps instead of condition polling
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.25 review. This is the real fix that .25 only bought headroom against.

.25 serialised the suite (--test-concurrency=1) to stop Chromium launch contention, which
works but costs 5x runtime (18s -> 88s). It does NOT remove the underlying fragility.

The suite has 106 page.waitForTimeout calls against only 2 page.waitForFunction calls, so
assertions race a fixed wall clock rather than waiting on the condition they care about.
Serialising merely lowers baseline load enough that the sleeps usually win.

Evidence: under 12 CPU-burner load at --test-concurrency=3, the failure was NOT the
waitForSelector timeout .25 describes. It was an assertion race:
  test/dim_highlight.test.js:250 "activeTermIndex === -1 ... dims every term"
  AssertionError: 0 !== 8

title: docs/privacy.html falsely claims nothing is added to the page DOM
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.10 review. This is the copy the Chrome Web Store Privacy tab links
to, so it is a disclosure accuracy problem, not a docs nit.

docs/privacy.html:141 states "Nothing is added to the page's DOM and nothing is sent
anywhere." The first half is false and always has been: content.js:2548 does
document.body.appendChild(wrap), and beacons and overlays append to document.documentElement
at content.js:809, 832, 858, 906, 1052, 1224, 1482, 1627 and others.

This sits in a "What the extension does" section that has NO counterpart in PRIVACY.md, so it
is also the one real content drift between the two files.

Predates this epic. Done: the claim describes what the extension actually injects, and the
section either gains a PRIVACY.md counterpart or the drift is deliberate and noted.

title: Overlay panels lack aria-haspopup/aria-expanded and never move focus into the dialog
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.9 review. Consistency issue across the whole overlay, not a .9
regression, but it matters more here than in most codebases: this is an accessibility extension.

Both listsBtn and the pre-existing gearBtn have aria-label and title but no aria-haspopup and
no aria-expanded, so a screen reader user gets no signal that the control opens a panel or
that the panel is currently open. Opening either role="dialog" panel also moves no focus into
it, so the panel's controls are announced only if the user goes hunting.

Done: both buttons expose aria-haspopup and a live aria-expanded; opening a panel moves focus
into it and returns focus to the trigger on close; a test asserts the announced state.

title: saveList accepts an empty terms array, so loading that list wipes the working list
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.9 review. Storage-layer wart from .8, first reachable through .9's UI.

saveList does not reject an empty terms array, so with zero chips a user can save a list
containing 0 terms. Loading that list later silently replaces the working list with nothing,
and since loading deliberately has no confirmation, the user loses their current terms with
no way back.

Done: saveList rejects an empty terms array, or the UI disables "Save current as..." when the
working list is empty. A test covers save-with-zero-chips.

title: Playwright suite flakes under parallel load
description:
Observed repeatedly across the v1.7.0 epic by more than one agent, in different beads.

Symptom: an entire run fails with waitForSelector timeouts on '#oc-wrap >> .oc-input' across
several unrelated suites at once (chip_row, prefers_reduced_motion, list_storage,
popover_width have all been seen). Re-running the same suite passes. It is Chromium launch
contention under `node --test test/*.test.js`, which runs files in parallel, not a defect in
any one bead.

Cost: it makes every "npm test passes" claim in this epic slightly less trustworthy, and it
will keep costing rerun time.

Fix direction: serialise the browser-backed suites, share one browser context across files,
or raise the launch timeout.

Done: ten consecutive full-suite runs pass without a rerun.
notes: Raised P3 -> P2 by the orchestrator and taken first in the follow-up run. Rationale: this is the only bead that degrades confidence in every other bead's verification. Nine reviewer PASSes in this epic rested on 'npm test passes', and at least three agents observed spurious full-suite failures under Chromium launch contention. Fixing it first makes the remaining follow-up reviews trustworthy.

title: Lite Mode: restoreActiveChip can land on a sparse placeholder
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.7 review.

restoreActiveChip (content.js:2240) reads termRanges[activeTermIndex] without checking it
holds real Range objects. Under Lite Mode, inactive terms are stored as a sparse
new Array(count) placeholder rather than real ranges.

Repro: in Lite Mode, removeChipAt (content.js:2460-2476) can shift activeTermIndex onto a
placeholder entry without triggering a rescan. A later draft-then-clear then restores that
chip and shows "0 of N" with zero highlights on the page, because the forEach at
content.js:2249 skips the holes.

Done: restoreActiveChip rescans when the active term's entry is not real ranges; a test
covers remove-then-restore under Lite Mode.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: RESOLVED AS ALREADY-FIXED, not by a new guard. Investigation for this bead found the stated repro no longer reproduces: oculist-l6m.33 (commit 8b530ec) made removeChipAt call performListSearch(), which is exactly the 'without triggering a rescan' precondition the repro depended on. Reviewer independently enumerated every activeTermIndex writer (activateChip, addChipTerm, removeChipAt, loadSavedList, __ocDestroy, loadWorkList) and confirmed each is followed by a synchronous materializing rescan, that performListSearch materializes the active slot before the cap loop so TOTAL_MATCH_CAP cannot starve it, and that starved slots are whole holes rather than sparse arrays. A defensive isPlaceholderRangeList guard was written and then deliberately DELETED: its branch was unreachable, its test provably could not discriminate (passed against unfixed code), and its comment block documented a splice-then-rescan interleaving window that does not exist. Shipped instead: a three-line comment at content.js:2521 documenting the real invariant (performListSearch is the only thing that materializes the active slot; every activeTermIndex writer must call it synchronously), plus test/lite_mode_restore.test.js as a regression pin on that invariant. Suite 97 pass / 0 fail.

title: findNext bypasses list ownership, wiping dim highlights and desyncing nav
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.5 review, both cases reproduced live. Nothing in the epic backlog
owns the findNext-versus-list ownership boundary; this bead does.

findNext() still routes through performSearch(), which knows nothing about the term list, so
navigating matches can tear down list state that performListSearch() built.

CASE 1 — dim highlights wiped by navigation (content.js:2325-2331)
With a zero-match active chip, a second Enter (or Ctrl+G / next) falls through to
findNext -> performSearch, which deletes oculist-dim-match. Observed dim ranges going 3 -> 0
after committing 'zebra' then pressing Enter. Chip counts survive; dim returns only on the
next scan.

CASE 2 — nav state desyncs after a restore (content.js:2136-2183 vs :2315-2325)
After clearing the input restores a chip, the UI shows "0 of 3" with nav ENABLED, but
Enter/next/prev hit findNext's empty-term early return, which blanks the count and disables
nav while the 3 highlights stay lit on the page. Partly pre-existing via activateChip, newly
reachable through the restore path added in .5.

Fix direction: findNext needs to respect list ownership rather than assuming input.value is
the search term. Likely it should operate on searchRanges/termRanges directly when a list is
active, instead of re-deriving the term from the input.

Done: navigating with a list active never deletes oculist-dim-match; the count and nav
enabled-state always agree with what is highlighted; tests cover both cases above.

title: Dim treatment should key off contrast, not profile name
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.6 review, with a concrete failing case.

.6 gates the dotted-underline dim treatment on settings.visionProfile === 'low-vision' and
gives every other profile the 35% alpha wash. The reviewer confirmed an alpha wash shifts
lightness and saturation but NOT hue, so it cannot introduce a red-green or blue-yellow
confusion, and the colour-blind palettes' hue separation survives it.

The real failure is tritanopia: its match colour #ffcbd1 is already near-white, so 35% of it
blends to about rgb(255,237,239), roughly 1.02:1 against a white background. Effectively
invisible. Any pale custom colour has the same problem.

Fix direction: do not extend the underline branch by profile name. Gate it on the BLENDED
dim colour's contrast against the background, which catches tritanopia and pale custom
colours automatically. prefers-contrast: more is currently unused anywhere in the extension
and would be a reasonable second trigger.

Done: dim is visible under every built-in profile including tritanopia, verified by measured
contrast rather than by eye.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: BLOCKED ON A DESIGN DECISION - left in_progress with work uncommitted in the tree on branch v1.6.0. Implementation of the specified mechanism is complete and correct (profile-name check removed, measured-contrast gate at 3:1 per WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11, prefers-contrast:more as an independent second trigger, computed once per settings/search event in injectHighlightStyles, never per range; suite 104 pass / 0 fail). Reviewer returned NEEDS-WORK because the bead's actual done-criterion is not met. THE FINDING: the code measures the branch it rejects and never the branch it selects. content.js:4751 paints the underline in full-strength matchColor. Against a white page that is 1.164:1 for #fef08a (none/low-vision/deuteranopia/protanopia/warm) and 1.427:1 for #ffcbd1 (tritanopia - the exact case this bead exists to fix). Tritanopia goes from 1.13:1 invisible to 1.43:1 invisible: a measured improvement, not measured visibility. THE MATH, derived independently: at alpha 0.35 the max achievable contrast is 2.4415:1 for pure black over white, and sweeping every grayscale background gives a per-profile ceiling of 2.939:1 (#fef08a), 2.617:1 (#ffcbd1), 2.085:1 (#f59e0b fallback). No built-in profile can clear 3:1 at alpha 0.35 against ANY background, light or dark. The alpha-wash branch is therefore unreachable for every built-in profile everywhere; it survives only for custom colours. Consequence: shipping as-is makes the dotted underline the universal dim treatment for all built-in profiles on all backgrounds. Note the bead's own ~1.02:1 figure for tritanopia was wrong; the correct value is 1.1298:1 (the bead's own rounded blend 255,237,239 computes to 1.1283:1). WHY RAISING ALPHA OR LOWERING THE THRESHOLD DO NOT WORK: #fef08a is 1.164:1 and #ffcbd1 is 1.427:1 against white at FULL opacity, so no alpha value reaches 3:1, and lowering the threshold just preserves a wash that genuinely does not read. The real fix is to derive the dim treatment's COLOUR so it clears 3:1 (darken matchColor toward the background's opposite until the underline measures) - that is a design change beyond this bead's stated direction, filed separately. Awaiting operator decision.

title: Chip hit counts are invisible to screen readers
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.4 review. Matters more than usual: this is an accessibility
extension.

.oc-chip-count is aria-hidden="true", and the chip term button's aria-label omits the
count. Bead .4 made those numbers meaningful (they are how a user knows which terms hit on
this page), but a screen reader user cannot reach them at all. They can hear the term and
nothing else.

Done: the count is exposed to assistive tech, most likely folded into the term button's
aria-label (e.g. "peanut, 3 matches"), with the visual span left aria-hidden to avoid a
double read. A test asserts the accessible name includes the count.

title: Zero-chip fallback leaves termRanges misaligned with workListTerms
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.4 review. Produces a wrong count on screen.

With no chips, performListSearch() substitutes [lastTerm] as an implicit single term, then
assigns termRanges length 1 while workListTerms is length 0.

Repro:
1. No chips. A mutation rescan fires with lastTerm === 'cat' -> termRanges = [7 ranges]
2. User types 'dog' (the draft path calls performSearch, which never touches termRanges)
3. User presses Enter -> the new 'dog' chip renders the count 7

Self-heals on the next scan, but the user sees a number that belongs to a different term.

Done: termRanges stays aligned with workListTerms in the zero-chip path; a test covers the
add-after-mutation-rescan sequence.

title: One dismissed notice permanently silences both term caps
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.3 review. Pre-existing behaviour, newly load-bearing.

showNotice() returns early forever once noticeDismissed is set (content.js:2037). That flag
is session-scoped, so a user who dismisses ANY notice once (including the site-override
notice) will never again see either term-cap message:
- "Oculist searches up to 10 terms at once. Remove a term to add another."
- "Search terms are limited to 100 characters. Shorten the term and try again."

The user then hits the 10-term cap and terms are silently refused with no explanation,
which reads as the extension being broken.

Fix direction: noticeDismissed should suppress only the notice class it was dismissed for,
or cap notices should bypass the flag since they are direct responses to a user action
rather than ambient advice.

Done: dismissing a site-override notice does not suppress a later cap notice; a test covers it.

title: List menu popover UI
description:
The overlay surface for saved lists. Reuses the existing settings-panel popover styling and
the shadow-root pattern.

Steps:
1. Add a list button to the oc-bar that toggles a popover.
2. Popover contents in order: "Save current as..." (prompts for a name and saves the
   working list), then the saved lists newest first, each with rename and delete controls.
3. Clicking a saved list loads it into the working list, replacing the current one with no
   confirmation. This is deliberate: "Save current as..." sits directly above the list so
   the save path is one click away.
4. Loading a list resets counts to blank and does NOT scan. The user clicks a chip to scan,
   matching the carry-over behaviour on a new page.
5. Accessibility: the popover is keyboard navigable and dismissible with Escape without
   tearing down the whole overlay, carries accessible names, and follows the existing theme
   variables and reduced-motion setting.
6. The popup (popup.html / popup.js) stays untouched.

Edge cases: opening the list menu while the settings panel is open must close the settings
panel, and the reverse. Escape inside the popover closes only the popover; a second Escape
closes the overlay as today. Saving with an empty name is rejected.

Done: a test covers save-then-load replacing the working list without triggering a scan,
and Escape closing only the popover.
notes:
FROM .8 REVIEW — obligation this bead inherits: saveList/renameList return {ok:false, reason:'empty-name'} SILENTLY, with no notice, which is correct layering for a storage function. Your 'Save current as...' prompt must therefore not treat that as a no-op. Disable the confirm control on blank/whitespace input, or keep the prompt open with inline validation. A silent dismissal is a real dead end for the user.

Storage signatures available to you (all take an optional callback):
  listSavedLists(callback)         -> callback(Array<{id, name, terms}>)
  saveList(name, terms, callback)  -> callback({ok:true, list} | {ok:false, reason})
  renameList(id, name, callback)   -> callback({ok:true, list} | {ok:false, reason})
  deleteList(id, callback)         -> callback({ok:true} | {ok:false, reason})
reason values: 'empty-name' (silent), 'cap' (shows notice), 'write-failed' (shows notice),
'not-found' (silent), 'exception' (silent).

title: Saved-list storage CRUD (per-key sync storage)
description:
Storage layer only. No UI in this task.

Steps:
1. Store each saved list under its own chrome.storage.sync key 'oc-list-<id>', shape
   {id, name, terms}. One key per list, NOT a single array: sync caps one item at 8192
   bytes, and per-key writes avoid the read-modify-write race when two devices save at once.
2. Implement listSavedLists() via chrome.storage.sync.get(null) filtered by the 'oc-list-'
   prefix, saveList(name, terms), renameList(id, name), deleteList(id), and an id generator.
3. Caps: 50 lists, 10 terms per list, 100 characters per term.
4. Every write checks chrome.runtime.lastError. Messages via showNotice():
   - 51st list: "You've saved 50 lists, the maximum. Delete one to save a new list."
   - write failure: "Couldn't save this list. Chrome's sync storage is full; delete a saved list and try again."
5. Do not touch 'oc-settings', SETTINGS_KEYS, or the pendingSelfWrites echo suppression.

Edge cases: a duplicate list name is allowed (ids are the identity); a rename to an empty
or whitespace-only name is rejected; deleting a list that is currently loaded leaves the
working list alone.

Done: a test round-trips save / list / rename / delete through per-list keys, asserts the
50-list cap message, and asserts a simulated chrome.runtime.lastError produces the sync
failure message.

title: Performance guards and Lite Mode count-only path
description:
Bound the cost of running getClientRects once per term.

Steps:
1. Keep the existing 999-matches-per-term cap. Add a 2000-match total cap across all terms.
   Once hit, stop materialising remaining inactive terms and call showNotice() with
   "Showing the first 2000 matches. Remove a term for a complete count."
   The active term is materialised first so it is never the one starved.
2. When settings.performanceMode (Lite Mode) is on, count inactive terms with a plain
   indexOf loop over normalizedFlatText and never build Range objects for them. No dim
   highlights in Lite Mode.
3. Lite Mode counts are computed before the visibility filter, so they can exceed what
   activating the chip shows. Activating a chip recomputes that term's count exactly and
   updates the chip.
4. Mark the deliberate ceiling with a ponytail comment naming the upgrade path.

Edge cases: toggling Lite Mode while a list is active must re-run the scan and add or drop
dim highlights accordingly. The total cap must count the active term's matches too.

Done: tests assert no Range objects are built for inactive terms under Lite Mode, that a
fixture exceeding the total cap fires the notice, and that activating a chip corrects its
count.
notes:
TEST HARNESS NOTE (from oculist-l6m.1 review): test/ has two patterns. Behavioural tests that need real layout or the CSS Custom Highlight API use Playwright + real Chromium (see test/spa_navigation.test.js, which serves a fixture over node:http and drives chromium). jsdom tests are for logic with no layout dependency. buildPageIndex/findRanges are IIFE-internal and NOT importable, so anything asserting on ranges, counts, getClientRects visibility filtering, or CSS.highlights registries must use the Playwright pattern. Use jsdom only for pure storage logic.
FROM .6 AND .5: the dim-building code is one function, updateDimHighlight(), but it now has THREE call sites, not one: performListSearch(), performDraftSearch(), and restoreActiveChip(). If Lite Mode should suppress dimming during draft typing and chip restore as well as committed scans, guard all three.

title: Dim highlight registry for inactive terms
description:
Show inactive terms' matches in a muted style.

Steps:
1. Add a third CSS.highlights registry, 'oculist-dim-match', holding the union of every
   inactive term's ranges.
2. Set explicit Highlight.priority values: dim = 0, oculist-match = 1,
   oculist-active-match = 2. This is required, not cosmetic: terms overlap (cat matches
   inside cats) and without priorities the last-registered registry wins, which can render
   the active term dim.
3. Style ::highlight(oculist-dim-match) as matchColor at 35% alpha over the existing text
   colour, derived from the same colour source as the existing match style so custom and
   colour-blind palettes flow through.
4. When settings.visionProfile is a low-vision or high-contrast preset, dim instead uses
   full matchColor with a dotted underline and no background wash, because a 35% wash
   defeats the contrast those presets exist to provide.
5. Delete all three registries in window.__ocDestroy and wherever the existing two are
   cleared.

Edge cases: CSS.highlights and Highlight are undefined in jsdom and on older Chrome, so
every touch stays inside the existing typeof/try-catch guards. A term that is both active
and duplicated must not appear in dim.

Done: a test asserts the dim set excludes the active term's ranges and that teardown clears
all three registry names.
notes: TEST HARNESS NOTE (from oculist-l6m.1 review): test/ has two patterns. Behavioural tests that need real layout or the CSS Custom Highlight API use Playwright + real Chromium (see test/spa_navigation.test.js, which serves a fixture over node:http and drives chromium). jsdom tests are for logic with no layout dependency. buildPageIndex/findRanges are IIFE-internal and NOT importable, so anything asserting on ranges, counts, getClientRects visibility filtering, or CSS.highlights registries must use the Playwright pattern. Use jsdom only for pure storage logic.

title: Draft input versus active chip ownership
description:
Define who owns searchRanges while the user is typing.

Rules to implement in content.js:
1. A non-empty input holds a DRAFT term that is not yet a chip. The draft owns searchRanges
   and the active highlight, so live debounced typing behaves exactly as it does today.
2. While a draft is active, chips stay rendered with their last known counts and their
   terms stay in the dim registry.
3. Committing the draft with Enter, or clicking a chip, hands ownership back to the list.
4. Clearing the input restores the previously active chip: its ranges become searchRanges
   again and its highlight returns, without a beacon animation.

Edge cases: clearing the input with no chips present must produce today's empty state
(blank count, nav disabled). Typing a draft identical to an existing chip's term must not
create a duplicate on Enter, it activates that chip. Rapid type-then-clear must not leave
a stale highlight registry entry.

Done: tests cover draft-then-clear restoring the active chip, and draft-equals-existing-chip
activating rather than duplicating.
notes:
FROM .4 REVIEW (defensive, likely your territory): a restored list with activeTermIndex === -1 and an empty input now lets rescanAfterMutation through, which writes 'no match' and fires checkSiteOverride(true), producing an unsolicited 'No matches found' notice on text-heavy pages. Not reachable via current persistence paths, but this bead owns the draft/active-chip ownership rules that would make it reachable.
SCOPE ADDITION — BLOCKING, from the .6 review. The epic's headline behaviour does not work on the primary flow, and this bead owns the fix.

REPRO on the current branch: open the overlay, type 'cat' and press Enter, then type 'dog' and press Enter. Result: CSS.highlights.has('oculist-dim-match') is false, oculist-match holds only 'dog' ranges, and the chips render with NO per-term counts. Dim highlights and counts appear only after a chip click (activateChip) or a DOM mutation rescan.

CAUSE: addChipTerm (content.js:2326-2329) does not rescan, and the Enter path falls through to findNext -> performSearch (content.js:2215), which deletes all three highlight registries and rebuilds only oculist-match.

This is exactly the ownership handoff this bead is about: 'committing the draft with Enter hands ownership back to the list'. Today it does not. Committing a draft with Enter must run performListSearch (not bare performSearch) so dim highlights and every chip count are present after a single Enter.

Required test: type term A, Enter, type term B, Enter, then assert WITHOUT any chip click that oculist-dim-match exists and contains A's ranges, and that both chips show numeric counts.

title: Chip row UI and working-list state
description:
Add the chip row to the overlay. Counts are out of scope here (blank placeholders); the
scan that fills them lands in the performListSearch task.

Steps:
1. Render a chip row inside the shadow root beneath the oc-bar input. Hidden entirely when
   terms is empty, so the zero-chip overlay is visually identical to today.
2. Each chip shows its term, a count slot, and a remove control.
3. Enter handling in keydownHandler: if input.value is non-empty and differs from the
   active chip's term, add it as a chip and make it active, then fall through to the
   existing findNext() call. Otherwise Enter is next-match exactly as today. Do not clear
   the input.
4. Adding a term already present activates that chip instead of duplicating.
5. Backspace in an empty input removes the last chip.
6. Clicking a chip sets activeTermIndex.
7. Caps with showNotice() messages:
   - 11th term: "Oculist searches up to 10 terms at once. Remove a term to add another."
   - over 100 chars: "Search terms are limited to 100 characters. Shorten the term and try again."
8. Persist the working list on every mutation via saveWorkList(); restore it on overlay
   mount via loadWorkList() and render the chips WITHOUT running any scan.
9. Accessibility: chips are keyboard reachable, carry accessible names including the term,
   use the existing theme CSS variables and vision-profile sizing, and have no animation
   under the reduced-motion setting.

Edge cases: terms containing only whitespace are rejected silently; leading/trailing
whitespace is trimmed before the duplicate check; removing the active chip moves active to
the previous chip, or to none if the list empties.

Done: tests cover add / duplicate / backspace-remove / both caps / restore-without-scan.
notes:
FOLLOW-UPS from oculist-l6m.2 review, handle in this bead:
1. loadWorkList has a latent double-invoke: on the synchronous unavailable-storage path, if the caller's callback throws, the outer catch calls that same callback again with the default. Unreachable until this bead adds the first consumer. Guard it.
2. activeIndex is validated only as typeof === 'number', so NaN and out-of-range values round-trip unchecked. This bead must range-check activeIndex against terms.length when restoring.
3. Call loadWorkList/saveWorkList directly from inside the IIFE closure. Do NOT add more window.__oc* hooks; the two that exist are for test reachability only.

title: performListSearch() and per-term counts
description:
Wire the chip list to the search engine.

Steps:
1. Add performListSearch(): call buildPageIndex() once, then findRanges(index, term) for

title: Add 4 elemental candidates (Round 5) to effects-playground.html
description:
Add a new 'Round 5' of 4 candidate effects to artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html — one per classical element (Fire, Water, Earth, Air) — following the exact conventions established by the existing 26 effects (Rounds 1-4) already in that file.

Read the file first, especially the Round 4 section (fxImpactburst, fxSpeedlines, fxShattercrack, fxHardfreeze near the end of the effect functions, and the effectsRegistry/buildSidebar code at the bottom) for the current shape of the conventions before writing anything.

Conventions to follow (same as every prior round):
- Effect = `function fxName(r) { ... }`, `r` is the shared `#match` element's rect.
- Every element you create gets `className` including `'fx'`, mounted via the existing `mount(el)` helper.
- Self-clean via your own `setTimeout` + `.remove()` — don't rely solely on `clearFx()` (that's the rapid-retrigger safety net, not your primary cleanup path).
- If an effect needs to temporarily mutate page-wide state (body transform, mark text color, etc.), capture/restore it via `addRestorer`/`removeRestorer` (see fxGravity or fxZoompunch for the pattern). Prefer not mutating page-wide state at all unless the effect genuinely needs it.
- Naming: function `fxCapitalizedsquashedname` (e.g. `fxImpactburst`, `fxHardfreeze` — capitalize only the first letter, no inner camelCase), registry key = same name lowercased with no `fx` prefix.
- Register all 4 in `effectsRegistry` after the existing 26 entries, in the same `{ label: '...', run: fxWhatever }` shape.
- Extend `buildSidebar()`'s round-slicing so a 'Round 5' divider appears after 'Round 4', containing exactly these 4, using `addDivider('Round 5', round5)` after the existing `addDivider('Round 4', round4)` call — don't change how rounds 1-4 are computed/labeled.
- Use the existing `Z` constant (2147483645) for z-index, same as every other effect.
- No autoplay on load — fires only via sidebar button click or 'Replay last', same as all existing effects.

IMPORTANT DEPARTURE from Round 4's design language: Round 4 effects were deliberately short (~150-350ms) and hard-edged/flat-colored to read as anime 'impact frames'. These 4 elemental effects should NOT follow that template — each should move at whatever pace and visual texture suits its element, per the approved design below. Some will run longer and softer than anything in Round 4, and that's intentional, not a bug.

Build these 4, per the approved design:

1. **Fire — "Ember Ignite"** (`fxEmberignite` / key `emberignite`) — total runtime ~700ms. A flame-silhouette shape (e.g. a rounded teardrop/blob built with border-radius or clip-path) rises from the match, with a warm gradient from deep red at the base to yellow/white at the tip. Flicker the flame's opacity and a slight horizontal skew/scaleX across 2-3 short cycles during its life (not a single smooth animate — genuinely wobble, e.g. via multiple keyframes with alternating small offsets) so it reads as an unstable flame rather than a static glowing shape. Also emit 3-4 small ember/spark particles that drift upward with slight horizontal drift (not perfectly straight), shrinking and fading as they rise. Soft/glowing edges (box-shadow or blur-ish gradient), not flat — fire should look hot.

2. **Water — "Ripple Surge"** (`fxRipplesurge` / key `ripplesurge`) — total runtime ~1000ms. 2-3 concentric ring outlines (border-radius circles, transparent fill, colored border) expand outward from the match center on an ease-out curve (fast start, decelerating, like a real ripple), fading opacity as they grow, staggered slightly so they don't perfectly overlap. Also one droplet element that arcs upward from the match then falls back with a small bounce/settle at the end (a simple 2-phase animation: rise+fall via a parabolic-feeling easing, then a quick small bounce). Translucent blue/cyan, soft edges — water should look wet and fluid, not solid.

3. **Earth — "Rockfall Thud"** (`fxRockfallthud` / key `rockfallthud`) — total runtime ~650ms (~120ms hard impact phase, ~500ms settle phase). Start with a quick heavy 'impact' cue: a brief sharp downward jolt on a small area around the match (e.g. a fast translateY snap-down-then-up on a couple of rock-shard elements, or a very brief page-local shake if you want, but keep any page-wide mutation properly restored via addRestorer if you use one — a self-contained local jolt on your own new elements is simpler and preferred). Then 4-6 angular rock/debris shard fragments (small irregular polygons via clip-path, or simple rotated rectangles/triangles) pop outward and arc back down under a gravity-like ease-in fall, settling near the ground line. Also a low dust-puff cloud (1-2 soft low-opacity flattened ellipses) expanding and fading at the base. Matte, mostly-opaque earthy colors (browns/grays), minimal glow — earth should feel heavy and solid, not glowy.

4. **Air — "Gust Swirl"** (`fxGustswirl` / key `gustswirl`) — total runtime ~600ms. 2-3 thin curved wind-streak strokes (e.g. thin elongated divs with border-radius to fake a curve, or a small set of short rotated segments approximating a curve) swirl around the match in a spiral/orbit-like path and drift off past its edges, fading as they exit. Add 1-2 small drifting particles (tiny dots/dashes) caught in the current, moving along a gentle curved path. Pale, low-opacity, thin/wispy — air should feel light and barely-there, not solid or saturated.

Colors (keep each element visually unambiguous from the others and from all prior rounds):
- Fire: warm red-to-yellow gradient (e.g. base `#dc2626`/`#b91c1c` to tip `#facc15`/`#fde047`)
- Water: blue/cyan (e.g. `#0ea5e9` or `#06b6d4`), translucent
- Earth: brown/stone gray (e.g. `#78716c` or `#92400e`), mostly opaque
- Air: pale gray-white or very light blue (e.g. `#e2e8f0` or `#f1f5f9`), low opacity throughout

Edge cases:
- Each effect must be independently replayable in rapid succession without leaking elements (same standard as every prior round) — verify `.fx` count returns to its pre-fire baseline after each effect's own cleanup timeout, not just relying on clearFx().
- Don't reuse colors across the 4 elements in a way that makes them hard to tell apart.
- No new dependencies, no build step — this file stays a single self-contained HTML file like it already is.

Verification (no test suite exists for this prototype file):
- Load the file in a browser (this repo's playwright devDependency works for a scripted check), click each of the 4 new Round 5 sidebar buttons, confirm zero console errors, confirm each effect visibly does something distinct from the others (sample computed opacity/transform mid-animation for at least the flame flicker and the ripple rings to confirm they're actually animating, not just present in the DOM), and confirm `.fx` node count returns to baseline within ~1.5s of each firing.
- Spot-check 2 pre-existing effects from different earlier rounds (e.g. Sonar Ping from Round 1, Impact Burst from Round 4) still fire correctly and Round 1-4 grouping is untouched.
- No changes to any file outside artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html.

title: Honour OS-level prefers-reduced-motion when choosing beacon motion
description:
Oculist honours its own motionSensitivity setting (visionSettings.motionSensitivity: full | reduced | off) but never checks the OS-level prefers-reduced-motion media query. A user who has asked their operating system to reduce motion still gets full beacon animations unless they separately find and change the extension setting.

Original scope also covered capping flash opacity on the Impact Burst / Speed Lines effects; those effects were reverted in 2554612 and 1b9f7de, so that half no longer applies (see closed oculist-kd7).

Remaining work: treat window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') as a downgrade-only signal on the motion mode read in content.js — drawActiveOverlays() (~1567) and animate() (~1607) both compute the same value. When the OS asks for reduced motion, 'full' becomes 'reduced'; an explicit 'reduced' or 'off' is left alone, so the setting can only ever reduce motion further, never override the OS upward. Must react to the media query changing at runtime, not just at load.
close_reason: Implemented in 0f89a22 on branch v1.6.0. Shared effectiveMotion() in extension/content.js downgrades 'full' to 'reduced' when matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') matches; explicit 'reduced'/'off' untouched. Regression test test/prefers_reduced_motion.test.js flips the emulated preference at runtime and asserts the beacon part count drops and restores; verified it fails without the fix. Full suite: 22/22 pass.

description:

Do NOT create a new file or a new grid/card layout — extend this existing file with a new 'Round 4' of 4 additional candidates, following its established conventions exactly.

Existing conventions to match (read the file first, don't guess):

Prefer NOT mutating page-wide state at all if your effect doesn't need to — simpler is fine here.
- Naming convention: function `fxCapitalizedsquashedname` (e.g. `fxZoompunch`, `fxDepthdive`, `fxMatchstrike` — capitalize only the first letter, rest of the compound name is lowercase, no inner camelCase), registry key is the same name lowercased with no prefix (e.g. `zoompunch`, `depthdive`).

- Sidebar grouping: `buildSidebar()` currently slices `window.EFFECTS` into round1 (first 10, no divider), round2 (next 5, 'Round 2' divider), round3 (remainder, 'Round 3' divider). Add a 'Round 4' divider for your 4 new entries — extend the slicing logic (e.g. `window.EFFECTS.slice(15, 19)` for round3 and `.slice(19)` for a new round4, or whatever indices are correct given the final registry order) and call `addDivider('Round 4', round4)` after the existing `addDivider('Round 3', round3)` call. Do not change how rounds 1-3 are computed/labeled.

- No autoplay on load — effects only fire via sidebar button click or the 'Replay last' button, exactly like the existing 22. Do not add a load-time autoplay for your 4.

Design intent (why these 4, and why they should look distinct from a generic 'glowing highlight'): these are 'impact frame' candidates, inspired by anime/manga impact-frame conventions — hard, SHORT, high-contrast hits rather than smooth glowing animations. Aim for roughly 150-350ms total runtime per effect (a handful of anime frames), near-instant snaps rather than long eased curves, and flat/hard-edged shapes (solid fills, bold outlines) rather than soft blurred gradients. This is a deliberate contrast with most of the existing 22 effects, which tend to be smoother/longer — that contrast is the point of this round.

Build these 4:
1. **Impact Burst** (`fxImpactburst` / key `impactburst`) — hard white flash (~60-80ms) + a flat-color jagged star/burst shape centered on the match that snaps to full size almost instantly and cuts off abruptly (no long fade).
2. **Speed Lines** (`fxSpeedlines` / key `speedlines`) — flat-color (not gradient) straight lines radiating from the match at evenly-spaced angles, snapping to full length fast, hard cutoff.
3. **Shatter Crack** (`fxShattercrack` / key `shattercrack`) — 8-14 jagged 2-segment 'crack' lines at randomized angles/lengths radiating from the match (mimicking a glass-crack impact), plus a quick flash. 4. **Hard Freeze Flash** (`fxHardfreeze` / key `hardfreeze`) — the most literal 'impact frame': a near-full-opacity flash across the viewport for ~2-3 frames (~80-120ms), plus a bold angular outline that snaps around the match at the same instant. Prefer `steps()` or a very short easing over long cubic-bezier curves.
