Recommend folding this into oculist-3z6 rather than tracking separately: the fix is condition polling instead of frame-count assertions, which is what oculist-l6m.32 did for the sleep-based tests.

title: Intermittent full-suite failure: strictEqual 1 !== 0, test name uncaptured
description: Observed once during the epic/oculist-dvt-cleanup final verification on 2026-08-28, AFTER the oculist-li8 concurrency cap (=4) landed: one full-suite run at OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3 failed a single assertion with code ERR_ASSERTION, strictEqual, actual 1, expected 0 - NOT the old LONG_TIMEOUT contention signature. Three other full-suite runs immediately around it were 206/206 green, so roughly 1-in-4 that session. The failing test's name was not captured (only the stack tail was seen). Plausible candidates are the new zero-leak assertions added this epic (test/waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js asserts 0 running animations and 0 .oc-beacon elements after cancel; several effect tests assert no .oc-beacon leaks), but this is unattributed - do not assume. NEXT STEP: run the full suite in a loop capturing per-run logs until the failure reproduces, then read the failing test name from the log and diagnose from there.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CAPTURED with a name during the oculist-5v9 review full-suite run (2026-08-28, concurrency=4, SCALE=3): the strictEqual 1 !== 0 failure is 'drawActiveMatchMagnifier: cancelBeacons() mid-flight...' in test/waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js - passed 32/32 when its file reran in isolation. Same run also had two other load flakes: 'removing the active first chip of several activates the new leftmost chip' (CDP Promise was collected) and 'an unscanned chip after a carry-over restore has no count in its accessible name' (timeout, chip_count_accessibility - also flaked once during the oculist-3ak implementation run). So the 0d2 signature is a load-contention race in the magnifier cancel subtest, not a product regression; the suite has grown ~10 Playwright files since the concurrency cap was tuned. Diagnosis should start at the magnifier subtest's post-cancel assertion (expected 0, got 1 - likely one animation still 'running' when sampled under CPU starvation, or a beacon element count).

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Root-caused and fixed as a test race, no product bug. Mechanism: setVisionSettings({magnifier:true}) is an OVERLAY_AFFECTING_KEYS change, so with an active match present the onChanged handler synchronously draws an incidental magnifier card; fireBeacon()'s waitForSelector resolved on that card while Enter's own redraw sat in a setTimeout(50); under load the assert slipped past t=50 and the deferred animate() resurrected the card after count===0 - hence strictEqual 1 !== 0, full-suite-only, ~1 in 4-8 runs. Fix: one cancelBeaconsMidFlight() between the settings change and fireBeacon(). Both implementer and reviewer reproduced the race deterministically (artificial post-cancel delay: fails 4/4 pre-fix, passes 4/4 post-fix at 150ms and 400ms); the fix also strengthens the subtest (snapshot now captures 25 running animations from the genuine Enter draw vs 2 stale ones before). Five full-suite runs green across both passes.

title: Lists panel has the same unbounded-height overflow as oculist-6cd
description: Found by the oculist-6cd reviewer: #oc-lists-panel (extension/content.js:6846-6862) has the same unbounded-height pattern the settings panel had - no max-height, host overflow hidden - so on short viewports the lists popover clips unreachably. Apply the same fix as oculist-6cd (max-height calc(100vh - bar chrome) + overflow-y auto) and cover it with a viewport-600 Playwright test at all four bar positions. Minor related notes from the same review, address while in there: the 44px barChromePx literal has ~3px slack and its comment credits the wrong tallest child (input.oc-input ~27px, not the 26px button); flex-shrink:0 on .oc-settings-header/.oc-settings-grid is currently inert, comments overstate it.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Premise correction discovered during implementation: the lists panel was not literally unbounded - it had a flat max-height:320px, which only clips unreachably on viewports shorter than ~360px (bar ~41px + 320px cap). At the bead's suggested vh=600 the old code never clipped. Fix replaces the flat cap with calc(100vh - barChromePx) matching oculist-6cd; regression test runs at vh=300 where old code demonstrably failed 4/4 positions (host bottom 361>300 top-anchored, host top -61 bottom-anchored). Also landed the 6cd review's comment corrections: barChromePx arithmetic now credits input.oc-input (~27px) as tallest bar child with 3px slack stated honestly, and the flex-shrink:0 comments no longer overstate an inert guard.

title: Nothing ties the effect enumerations to the registry
description:
Recommended by the oculist-dvt.6 re-reviewer, who noted this test would have caught that bead's own original miss.

Three prose sites now enumerate all 13 effects, plus one hardcoded count: extension/welcome.html:226 ('Choose from 13 effects - ...'), docs/index.html:497, docs/index.html:578. All four facts must be hand-synced against effectsRegistry (extension/content.js:685-699) and NOTHING in the suite ties them together. Adding a 14th effect silently makes four sites wrong, and a short stale list just looks like a list - only the numeric count reads as obviously wrong once it drifts.

This is exactly how the pre-existing Bloom/Trail omission survived unnoticed through two releases: both docs lists sat at 7 effects while the registry had 9.

FIX: one test that parses the i18n labels out of effectsRegistry in declaration order, then asserts each of the three prose sites contains all of them IN ORDER, and that the digit in 'N effects' equals the registry size. Model the label extraction on what the dvt.6 reviewer did. Keep it a static source scan like test/privacy_invariants.test.js - no browser needed.

DONE: adding a 14th registry entry without updating the three prose sites fails a test that names which site is stale.

title: extension/welcome.html effect list is stale (missing Bloom, Trail, and 4 new effects)
description: extension/welcome.html line 226 (prose) and the effect <select> options (lines ~291-297) enumerate only 6 effects (Spotlight, Anime Laser, Warp Drive, Inferno Flame, Lightning, Electron Cloud, Pointing Arrows) and are missing Bloom, Trail, Speed Lines, Chrono Tunnel, Light Cycle, Cyber-Vision. Also note: the <option value="hud"> is labelled 'Spotlight' in welcome.html but content.js's effectsRegistry maps hud -> effectAnimeLaser (Anime Laser runs on hud); value="iris" is the actual Spotlight effect. Worth checking if welcome.html's option values are stale/mismatched too. Out of scope for oculist-dvt.6 because extension/ is explicitly DO NOT TOUCH in that bead's brief.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION and description fixes, from the oculist-dvt.6 review. 1. The PROSE enumeration at extension/welcome.html:226 has been REMOVED from this bead's scope - it is being fixed inside oculist-dvt.6 itself, because it is a plain

of onboarding copy and the dvt.6 done-criterion covers 'every place in the repo that enumerates effects'. What remains here is only the functional either uses the real registry keys and labels, or carries a comment stating explicitly that its vocabulary is deliberately separate and non-persisting.

title: Settings panel overflows a 600px viewport regardless of effect count
description:
Measured precisely by the oculist-dvt.5 reviewer on 2026-08-28 with real Chromium geometry. PRE-EXISTING and independent of the effect registry's size: at the pre-epic commit bfaaca8 with only 9 effects, the panel host measured 686.4px tall, already 86.4px over a 600px viewport. oculist-dvt.5's scroll cap brought the 13-effect panel DOWN to 674.4px - shorter than the old 9-effect panel - so that bead fixed the regression it introduced but did not and should not have fixed this.

The failure is unrecoverable, not merely ugly: content.js:6218-6222 sets ':host { position: fixed; overflow: hidden }' with no max-height and no scrollable ancestor, so clipped content cannot be reached by any page scroll. Measured hostTop -74.4px at vh=600 with the bar bottom-anchored (bl/br) - the panel header and first rows sit above the viewport. Top-anchored (tl/tr) loses the footer instead.

This bites real users on short windows, split-screen layouts, and laptops with browser chrome eating vertical space.

FIX: bound the PANEL, not just the effect list - a max-height on the panel tied to the available viewport height (with the bar's position taken into account, since bottom-anchored constrains upward) plus overflow-y auto, mirroring what dvt.5 did one level down. Check all four POS_DATA positions. DONE: at vh=600 every panel control is reachable at all four bar positions, with no clipped header or footer.

title: Beacon geometry assumes host pages do not set box-sizing: border-box
description:
Found by the oculist-dvt.4 re-reviewer while deriving the bracket geometry. Cyber-Vision's targeting brackets (extension/content.js:2847-2857) are content-box elements: width/height 15px plus a 2px border, so the surviving border sits OUTSIDE the declared width and the far edges land at pad + 2px. That is correct on the test fixture.

But Oculist injects into arbitrary host pages, and a very large fraction of real sites ship 'html, body, *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box }'. The extension's beacon elements are appended to document.documentElement, so a universal selector on the host page WILL match them. Under border-box the 2px border is drawn INSIDE the 15px, shifting every far edge in by 2px and making the brackets frame the match slightly differently than designed.

This is a PRODUCTION issue in content.js, not a test defect - the test correctly encodes what the code does today. Blast radius is cosmetic and small (2px, scaled by getBeaconScale, so 4.5px at xl), but it applies to any beacon element that relies on content-box sizing, not just Cyber-Vision's brackets - audit the others while here.

FIX: set an explicit 'box-sizing:content-box' (or border-box, chosen deliberately) in the cssText of beacon elements whose geometry depends on it, so host-page CSS cannot change their layout. The beacons already set position/pointer-events/z-index defensively for the same reason; box-sizing belongs in that set. DONE: bracket geometry is identical on a fixture that sets '* { box-sizing: border-box }' and one that does not.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Residual gap noted by the reviewer: the fix uses non-!important inline styles, so a host page shipping '* { box-sizing: border-box !important }' still overrides beacon geometry. The test fixture deliberately uses a realistic no-!important reset. Accepted scope for this bead.

title: Light Cycle applies getBeaconScale twice
description:
Found by the oculist-dvt.3 reviewer. animateLightCycle applies getBeaconScale() at BOTH levels: once as the container's transform scale(scale) (extension/content.js:2531) and again per child element - THICK = 3 * scale (:2536), headSize = 8 * scale (:2558), boxPad = 6 * scale (:2632, :2641). The established pattern in animateAnimeLaser (content.js:877) applies the container scale ONLY, with fixed child sizes.

Consequence: at beaconSize 'xl' (scale 2.25) the wall renders about 15px thick instead of the intended ~7px, i.e. scaled twice over. Nothing fails today because test/light_cycle.test.js never varies beaconSize - and note that 15px would also breach that test's own 'min(width,height) <= 10' right-angle threshold, so the bug is currently invisible only because the test runs at the default size.

FIX: drop the per-child scale multipliers and let the container transform do the work, matching animateAnimeLaser. Then extend the right-angle test to run at all four beacon sizes so the threshold is exercised where it actually bites. DONE: wall thickness at xl is proportionate, and the right-angle test passes at s/m/l/xl.

RELATED, same review, same file: midYVp = Math.min(vpCy + 96, window.innerHeight - 26) at content.js:2487 can land within a pixel of finalYVp (:2488) for a match low in the viewport, yielding a ~1px stub segment via Math.max(len, 1). Not reproduced on the test fixture, but a real geometry edge case worth guarding while in here.

title: WAAPI animations leak on every effect except Light Cycle
description:
Confirmed empirically by the oculist-dvt.3 reviewer in a clean Chromium page: after el.remove() a Web Animations API animation still reports playState 'running' with currentTime advancing (192.4ms to 601.0ms observed). Only Animation.cancel() stops it (playState 'idle', currentTime null). So removing a beacon element does NOT stop its animations - they keep ticking until GC.

oculist-dvt.3 fixed this for Light Cycle only: animateLightCycle collects its animations into container.__waapiAnims (extension/content.js:2668) and cancelBeacons() (content.js:835-839) cancels them. That block is guarded and is a strict no-op for every other effect, because NO OTHER EFFECT SETS __waapiAnims.

So the fix is half-adopted. animateTrail, animateAnimeLaser, animateLightning, animateIris, animateWarpDrive, animateFlame, animatePointingArrows, animateDispersion and drawActiveMatchMagnifier all drive WAAPI animations and all still leak them on cancel. Impact is bounded - the animations are short and the elements are detached, so it is wasted work rather than a visible bug - but it is real, and it is exactly the class of thing that compounds on a page where the user searches repeatedly.

FIX: hang __waapiAnims off each WAAPI effect's container the way animateLightCycle does. Mechanical and low-risk; the cancelBeacons() side already exists. DONE: firing each effect and calling cancelBeacons() mid-flight leaves no animation in playState 'running'.

title: speed_lines.test.js clear-lane test flakes under full-suite parallel load (elseMax starved of real animation frames)
Document the four new effects
description:
Bring the user-facing docs up to date with the 13-effect registry. Dependency-gated on the two chain tails so it documents the shipped reality, not the plan.

SCOPE:
1. CHANGELOG.md - add an entry for the four new effects following the existing Keep a Changelog format. Read the file's conventions first: a dated heading means RELEASED (established by commit 26d10f6 and confirmed during the oculist-l6m.10 review), so do NOT date the heading unless the operator is cutting a release. Check with the orchestrator rather than guessing the version number.
2. docs/index.html - THE EFFECT LIST HERE IS ALREADY STALE, independent of this epic. Line 497 and line 578 both enumerate only 7 effects (Anime Laser, Spotlight, Warp Drive, Inferno Flame, Lightning, Electron Cloud, Pointing Arrows) - they are missing Bloom and Trail, which already shipped. Fix that pre-existing omission AND add the four new ones, so both lists name all 13. Line 566 describes the picker generally and may need no change.
3. README.md line 12 names a few effects as examples rather than enumerating them; check whether it still reads correctly at 13 and leave it alone if so.

Do NOT touch PRIVACY.md or docs/privacy.html - no storage or permission behaviour changes in this epic, and test/privacy_invariants.test.js pins the claim they make.

DONE: every place in the repo that enumerates effects names all 13, the pre-existing Bloom and Trail omission in docs/index.html is fixed, and the CHANGELOG entry is undated unless the orchestrator says otherwise. A grep for the old 7-effect list returns nothing.

title: Settings panel at 13 effects: picker ergonomics
description:
The effect picker is makeRadioList (extension/content.js around 4062-4103), rendering one row per registry entry. This epic takes it from 9 rows to 13. Established behaviour: a row is marked active only on an exact item.value === currentVal match, and the panel is rebuilt via rebuildSettingsPanelPreservingFocus() on storage changes.

INPUT: all four new effects registered (this bead is dependency-gated on the two chain tails).

INVESTIGATE FIRST, then fix only what is actually broken. Do not restructure a panel that works:
1. Does the settings panel overflow the viewport at 13 rows, at each of the four beacon sizes and at the browser's larger default font sizes? The panel is inside the overlay's shadow root and is height-constrained by the find bar's position (top/bottom, left/right - see POS_DATA).
2. If it does overflow, is the fix a scroll container on the effect list, grouping the effects under headings, or a two-column layout? Prefer the smallest change that works. A scroll container is almost certainly it; grouping invents taxonomy the product does not have.
3. Does keyboard navigation still work end to end - can you reach the 13th row by keyboard, and does focus stay visible when the list scrolls? test/settings_panel_rebuild_focus.test.js and test/overlay_panel_focus_aria.test.js own this behaviour; check them before changing anything.
4. Does the panel still restore focus correctly after a rebuild with the longer list?

DONE: the settings panel is usable at 13 effects - no clipped rows, no unreachable options, keyboard navigation reaches every row, and focus behaviour after a rebuild is unchanged. A test covers whichever failure you actually found. If nothing is broken, say so explicitly, add a regression test pinning the panel's usability at the full registry length, and close it - a no-change outcome with evidence is a valid result here.

title: find_next_list_ownership and draft_ownership flake at LONG_TIMEOUT under load
description: Measured by the oculist-l6m.22 reviewer with a controlled A/B on 2026-08-27. Ten full-suite runs at OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3: five WITH the .22 diff were 149/149 green every time; five WITHOUT it (test/list_storage.test.js reverted) failed 2 of 5. The failures were test/find_next_list_ownership.test.js ('CASE 3 (regression)...') and test/draft_ownership.test.js ('a restored list with no active chip...'), both timing out at ~15080ms - exactly LONG_TIMEOUT (15000 x 3). So these two files flake under parallel load on stock main even at SCALE=3, which is the highest scale anyone is likely to run. The A/B direction rules out oculist-l6m.22 as the cause. NOTE the earlier oculist-rdx run observed a different but related contention flake in worklist_storage. FIX: find why these two need more than 15s of wall clock under load - either a genuinely slow path worth optimising, or a poll that should key off a condition rather than a deadline. Raising LONG_TIMEOUT is the last resort, not the first. DONE: 10 consecutive full-suite runs at SCALE=3 are green, or the slow path is identified and fixed.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Widening the observed set. Across the epic/oculist-l6m-v3 run (2026-08-27) these files have each flaked at least once at SCALE=3 in a full-suite run while passing in isolation immediately after: find_next_list_ownership.test.js, draft_ownership.test.js, color_picker_persistence.test.js, dim_highlight.test.js, list_search.test.js, worklist_storage.test.js, and resize_overlays.test.js (the last one timing out on page.waitForSelector for #oc-active-match-label at test/resize_overlays.test.js:135). So this is NOT confined to the two files in the title - it is a general full-suite contention problem that surfaces in whichever Playwright test happens to be scheduled under load. That reframes the fix: raising individual budgets will just move the flake around. Look instead at how many browser contexts the suite runs concurrently (node --test parallelism vs one launchPersistentContext per file) and whether limiting concurrency removes it outright. DONE unchanged: 10 consecutive full-suite runs at SCALE=3 green.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Resolved by capping node --test to --test-concurrency=4 in the npm test script. Root cause: 35 of 39 test files launch a real Chromium via launchPersistentContext, and node --test defaults to os.availableParallelism()=10 workers on this box, oversubscribing 10 cores and starving the deadline-based polls in test/helpers/wait.js. Evidence: 16 consecutive green full-suite runs at SCALE=3 post-fix (implementer 10 + reviewer 6), wall clock ~57s -> ~64s. Caveats from review: the causal link is inferential (the flake is intermittent; two pre-fix baseline runs were also green), and 4 is hardcoded per this 10-core box - revisit with an env override or availableParallelism()/2 before adding CI on different hardware.

title: termStarved splice alignment in removeChipAt is untested
description: Found by the oculist-l6m.21 reviewer via mutation. oculist-l6m.21 added a module-level termStarved array parallel to termRanges, carrying the per-chip 'skipped because the match cap was hit' flag that renders the em-dash marker. Every termRanges mutation site has a paired termStarved mutation, and the reviewer confirmed no reachable desync today. BUT: deleting the paired 'termStarved.splice(index, 1)' at extension/content.js:3455 (in removeChipAt) leaves the full suite GREEN - list_search + chip_row + chip_count_accessibility + worklist_storage + dim_highlight all pass 38/38 at SCALE=3. No test removes a chip after a starved scan, so a future edit could drop that splice and silently paint the em-dash marker on the WRONG chip. A wrong-chip marker is worse than no marker. Partly self-limiting: isStarved is gated on !hasCount, so a stale flag can only surface on a chip that is itself unscanned. FIX: add a case that trips the cap, removes a chip ahead of the starved one, and asserts the remaining chips keep their correct markers. DONE: deleting the termStarved splice at content.js:3455 fails a test.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Closed as premise-stale after independent implementer + reviewer verification on branch epic/oculist-cleanup-batch2 (2026-08-28). The termStarved.splice(index,1) in removeChipAt (content.js:4479) is causally inert: every path through removeChipAt that reaches the splice falls through to an unconditional synchronous performListSearch(), which REALLOCATES termRanges/termStarved (new Array(terms.length) or []) from post-splice workListTerms - prior contents can never survive. The only reader (renderChipRow, content.js:4654) is called only after those reallocations; removeChipAt never renders. Verified empirically twice: the bead's exact scenario (cap tripped, chip removed ahead of a starved chip) passes identically with and without the splice, and the full suite is 206/206 green under the mutation. So the demanded test (deleting the splice fails a test) is unsatisfiable without production changes. DECISION: keep the splice - it preserves the parallel-array invariant mid-function as a defense against future edits inserting a render or await before the rescan; removing it was judged not worth a bead. termRanges.splice at 4478 is inert by the same argument; workListTerms.splice is the real mutation. Residual theoretical path: performListSearch throwing before rebuild (unwrapped buildPageIndex/findRanges) - unreachable without injected faults and not a testable distinction.

title: oculist-e9u test premise went stale under the oculist-7z3 guard
description: The oculist-e9u regression test in test/settings_panel.test.js (~line 375) documents itself as exercising animate()'s render-time fallback (effectsRegistry[effectKey] || effectsRegistry.hud, content.js:2589) via the post-boot storage.onChanged sync path, whose comment calls that path 'the only route by which settings.effect can actually hold a stale/removed key like lens at animate()-time'. oculist-7z3 added a registry guard in exactly that path (content.js:6074), so settings.effect is now normalised to 'hud' BEFORE animate() ever sees 'lens'. The test still passes, but it now passes because HUD is legitimately selected - it no longer reaches the fallback branch it names. Found by the oculist-7z3 reviewer. Not a correctness bug: the 2589 fallback is still a real defence-in-depth guard, it just has no test driving it any more. FIX: either drive the fallback directly (set the effect key at animate() time, bypassing the now-guarded storage path) or rewrite the test's comment to describe what it actually pins now. DONE: the 2589 fallback is either covered by a test that fails when it is deleted, or explicitly documented as untested with the reason.

title: Remove the Lens beacon effect
description: User evaluated the Lens effect on real pages and it does not work well enough to keep - the DOM-clone approach loses ancestor-dependent styling, which was the known ceiling recorded in its ponytail comment when it was built (oculist-y6a). Remove it rather than pursue the captureVisibleTab upgrade path. SCOPE: delete animateLens and its ponytail comment block from extension/content.js, the effectLens i18n label, the lens registry entry (it is the last entry, so drop the now-dangling trailing comma on the preceding trail line), and the whole test/lens_effect.test.js file. Reword the comment in animateTrail that cites 'the same degrade animateLens uses' so it no longer references a deleted function. Check for helpers left orphaned by the deletion. MIGRATION IS ALREADY HANDLED: content.js:6302 coerces an unrecognised settings.effect to 'hud' on settings load, so a user persisted on 'lens' falls back automatically - verify this rather than assume it, since it is the only thing standing between the removal and a dead beacon for anyone who had Lens selected. DONE: no reference to lens or animateLens remains in extension/, the suite passes at its new lower count, and a stored effect of 'lens' still yields a working beacon.

title: Trail: add an absorption flash when the arrowhead reaches the match
description: The Trail effect (animateTrail, extension/content.js) currently ends with the arrowhead simply stopping on the match. Make the arrival read as an energy transfer: the arrowhead vanishes into the match and the match's own area flashes once, as if it absorbed the energy. Fires exactly on arrival (delay equal to the travel duration), a SINGLE decaying pulse sized to the match rect. Single pulse only, never a loop or strobe - WCAG 2.3.1. Lite Mode keeps the flash (it is the payoff of the effect) but drops the shadow blur. DONE: the flash element is positioned over the match rect, its animation is delayed by the travel duration so it cannot fire early, it runs exactly one iteration, Lite Mode still flashes, and no beacon elements leak.

title: Test timeout knob misses ~15 hand-rolled pollers with hardcoded budgets
description: oculist-1v7 added OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE and swept the 262 declarative timeout literals, but the knob does not reach pollers that hardcode their own budget. Reviewer found ~15: 'const deadline = Date.now() + 5000' and '{ timeout: timeoutMs || 5000 }' across 9 files, the two IN-PAGE 'Date.now() + 15000' deadlines at test/worklist_storage.test.js:244 and :302, and the local waitForCondition default at test/trail_effect.test.js:93 (a documented duplicate of the shared helper). THIS MATTERS: the only contention flake actually observed during the oculist-1v7 review was worklist_storage.test.js:230, which polls one of those in-page 15000ms deadlines - so SCALE=3 would NOT have prevented it. The knob currently cannot fix the one failure it was built for. FIX: route these through POLL_TIMEOUT/LONG_TIMEOUT from test/helpers/wait.js. The in-page ones need the scaled value passed into page.evaluate/waitForFunction as an argument, since process.env is not readable from page context. While here, two small items from the same review: (1) OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=-2 yields POLL_TIMEOUT=-10000 (instantly-expiring timeouts) instead of degrading to 1 - guard with a '> 0 ? scale : 1' check; (2) the wait.js comment has a garbled parenthetical, 'Set OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3 (e.g. npm test)', which drops the env prefix. DONE: every poller in test/ derives its budget from the shared constants, a negative or zero scale falls back to 1, and OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3 demonstrably raises the worklist_storage in-page deadline.

title: New beacon effect: Lens — circular magnifier over the real page content around the match
description: Prototype a new effectsRegistry entry (key 'lens', label 'Lens') that briefly magnifies the ACTUAL page content around the active match, not a re-rendered text card. NOTE: this is distinct from the existing drawActiveMatchMagnifier() (content.js:2113), which renders the match TEXT at 2.5x inside a styled card and absorbs the N-of-M counter. Lens magnifies real page pixels/DOM in place. APPROACH (settled for the prototype): clone the match's nearest block-level ancestor with cloneNode(true), mount the clone absolutely positioned over the original in the light DOM (NOT a shadow root, so host page CSS still applies to it), transform: scale(~2) with transform-origin at the match centre, and clip it to a circle with clip-path: circle(). Animate the lens in and out. KNOWN CEILING, mark it with a ponytail: comment - a DOM clone loses any styling that depends on ancestor selectors, so the lens can look subtly wrong on complex layouts. The pixel-accurate upgrade path is chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab (the manifest already has activeTab) cropped and scaled into the lens, at the cost of an async background round-trip and having to hide Oculist's own overlays before capture so they do not appear inside the lens. Do NOT build that for the prototype. HARD CONSTRAINTS: must not mutate or reflow the host page (clone only, never wrap or transform real nodes); the clone must be inert (pointer-events:none, aria-hidden='true', and strip id attributes from the clone so it cannot duplicate ids in the document); className 'oc-beacon' so cancelBeacons() sweeps it; honour getBeaconScale()/getBeaconDuration(); single pass, no loop (WCAG 2.3.1); remove itself on finish. Lite Mode should reduce or skip the blur/shadow trim. DONE: selectable in the settings panel, visibly magnifies real surrounding page content, a test asserts the clone carries the match text and is removed with no leak, a test asserts no duplicate ids are introduced into the document, and a test asserts the host page layout is unchanged while the lens is up. No fixed sleeps in tests (oculist-l6m.32).

title: New beacon effect: Trail — arrowhead travels an L-shaped path from the cursor to the match
description: Prototype a new effectsRegistry entry (key 'trail', label 'Trail') that draws a single arrowhead travelling an L-shaped (right-angle elbow) path from the user's last known cursor position to the active match rect, so the eye is led from where the hand is to where the hit is. Use the CSS motion-path primitives rather than hand-rolled keyframes: offset-path: path('M ...'), animate offset-distance 0%->100%, and offset-rotate: auto so the arrowhead turns to face travel direction at the elbow for free. Requires new mouse tracking: content.js has NO mousemove listener today. Add a passive document-level mousemove storing the last clientX/clientY, registered once at module scope, and removed in __ocDestroy alongside the existing resize/scroll listeners (content.js:691). KEY EDGE CASE: find-in-page is keyboard-driven, so the cursor may never have moved on the page and no position is known. Fall back to the find bar's own rect (that is where the user's attention is), and to viewport centre if the bar is somehow unavailable. Must honour getBeaconScale() and getBeaconDuration(), mount with className 'oc-beacon' so cancelBeacons() sweeps it, mount on document.documentElement in document space (cursor coords are viewport, so add scrollX/scrollY), pointer-events:none, and remove itself on finish. Single pass, no loop (WCAG 2.3.1). Lite Mode should skip the trailing line and draw the arrowhead alone. DONE: selectable in the settings panel, renders the travelling arrowhead, a test asserts the path starts at the tracked cursor position and ends at the match, a test asserts no beacon elements leak, and Lite Mode is respected. No fixed sleeps in tests (oculist-l6m.32).

title: Dispersion Bloom beacon effect: palette-derived radial chromatic dispersion
description: Add a new beacon effect to effectsRegistry (content.js:577) reproducing the look known in shader terms as radial chromatic dispersion / prismatic refraction / iridescent ripple. Design was brainstormed and specified 2026-08-26; only the final build approval was outstanding. DESIGN DECISION ALREADY MADE BY THE HUMAN: hues are DERIVED FROM THE ACTIVE PALETTE, not a true spectrum. A real R-G-B rainbow split conveys via hue, which is exactly what tritanopia/deuteranopia/protanopia users cannot separate, and Oculist's vision profiles exist to prevent that. So the effect splits around getEffectiveColors().beacon rather than the full spectrum: it stays colourblind-safe and consistent with the profiles, and reads as an iridescent dispersion bloom rather than a prism. Do not re-litigate this. SHAPE, mapping the three shader steps to DOM plus the Web Animations API: (1) UV distortion becomes an expanding ripple - three concentric rings centred on the match rect, scaling outward across getBeaconDuration(). (2) Channel offsetting becomes hue-offset rings - take getEffectiveColors().beacon, run it through hexToHsl, emit three rings at hue -22, 0, +22 degrees, the same idiom animateFlame already uses at content.js:1103-1106. Each ring gets a slightly different end scale and a small stagger, and that separation IS the dispersion. (3) Radial attenuation becomes progressive blur and fade - each ring animates filter: blur() outward while opacity falls, softening the separation toward the edge. (4) Additive recombination - the rings sit in a container with isolation: isolate and blend plus-lighter against each other ONLY, so they recombine bright at the core and split into iridescent bands at the fringe without blending into the host page, which would make the effect vanish on white backgrounds. Confirm plus-lighter against the manifest's Chrome floor (needs 111+) and fall back to screen if needed. NO WEBGL: this is a content script on arbitrary pages, every existing effect is DOM plus WAAPI, and a canvas adds compositing and CSP surface for something that fires once per active match. The isolate plus plus-lighter pairing reproduces the additive recombination a shader would do. WIRING is one function, one i18n label, one registry line - the in-page settings panel auto-enumerates effectsRegistry at content.js:3848, so no popup HTML change. INHERITED FREE, no code needed: animate() already returns early when motion is off and routes to animateReducedMotion when reduced, so this never fires under reduced motion; cancelBeacons() already sweeps .oc-beacon; and it enters no vision preset, so it is never auto-enabled. LITE MODE: three rings drop to one, matching warpDrive's ringCount = settings.performanceMode ? 1 : 3. DONE: the effect is selectable in the settings panel and renders a palette-derived dispersion bloom on the active match; a test asserts the ring hues track getEffectiveColors().beacon rather than a hardcoded spectrum when the profile changes; a test asserts all beacon elements are removed by the end (no leak); a test asserts reduced motion yields the reduced-motion beacon and never the rings; a test asserts Lite Mode drops the ring count. Use condition polling, not waitForTimeout - oculist-l6m.32 converted 156 fixed sleeps and a new one regresses it. Photosensitivity note: a single expanding pulse per activation, no repeat or flash, keeps this clear of WCAG 2.3.1's three-flash threshold; do not add looping or strobing.

title: Poll timeout budget of 5000ms is insufficient on contended hardware
description: Found during oculist-l6m.32 review. After the sleep-to-poll conversion (commit e97e029), parallel suite runs on a contended machine fail with isolated waitForFunction timeouts rather than wrong-value assertions: post-change 2/7/2 failures across three runs, versus pre-change 0/2/3. The failing test differed every run, and one failing file (chip_count_accessibility.test.js) is not touched by that diff at all, which points at the poll budget rather than at any specific conversion. test/helpers/wait.js defaults to a 5000ms timeout with a 30ms interval, and page.waitForFunction calls use Playwright's own default. The implementer deliberately declined to blanket-raise 5000ms to 10000ms on the grounds that a wide timeout increase masks real regressions, which is correct - a slow test that still passes tells you nothing. The right fix is probably not a global bump: consider a single configurable budget read from an env var so CI and contended dev boxes can raise it without changing what the suite asserts, leaving the default tight enough that a genuine regression still surfaces as a timeout quickly. MEASURE FIRST on an idle machine (this box was at load average 39-46 on 10 cores from unrelated work when the above numbers were taken) - the problem may not exist at all under normal conditions. Blocked-by relationship: resolving oculist-l6m.32's open load clause likely resolves or obviates this. Also fold in a small fix while here: test/chip_row.test.js:184's addTerm() helper gained an acceptance branch on 'any .oc-notice exists' which is load-bearing (4 cap/notice tests fail without it) but unscoped to the cap notice, so any test where a stray notice lingers gets a no-op wait. Scope the selector to the cap notice.

title: Malformed saved lists are invisible in the panel but still occupy one of the 50 list slots
description: Found during oculist-l6m.35 review. listSavedLists (content.js:263) excludes any entry failing its Array.isArray(entry.terms) shape guard, and readListIndex counts every oc-list-* key toward MAX_SAVED_LISTS regardless. So a corrupted entry (terms: 'nope', terms: null, a bare 'not-an-object' value, or a numeric id) is invisible in the saved-lists panel yet still consumes one of the 50 slots, with no way for the user to see or delete it. l6m.35 deliberately kept this conservative: its done-criteria were about the three gates agreeing on what 'empty' means, which is a different question from shape validation, and relaxing only the Array.isArray guard would fix roughly a quarter of the problem while leaving the other malformed shapes just as invisible. Needs a coherent policy decided as a whole: render anything carrying a usable id and name as a disabled row so rename/delete stay reachable, and/or stop counting unrenderable junk toward the cap. NOTE for whoever takes this: the pinned test 'listSavedLists() skips junk under the prefix instead of throwing' in test/list_storage.test.js documents old behaviour rather than encoding a deliberate contract - its real intent is 'does not throw', and its length === 1 assertion is a mechanical side effect of the shape check. Amend it rather than treating it as a blocker. Done: a malformed-but-identifiable saved list is either visible and deletable, or does not consume a slot; a test covers each malformed shape.

title: No change listeners on prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast or prefers-reduced-motion, so OS setting flips leave injected CSS stale
description: Found during oculist-l6m.28 review. All three media queries in content.js are poll-on-read with no change listener: getActiveThemeName() (content.js:545) reads matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches fresh per call, and prefersMoreContrastQuery (content.js:4691, from oculist-l6m.17) and reducedMotionQuery (content.js:2122) follow the same pattern. Confirmed by grep: no addEventListener('change') on any media query anywhere in content.js. Consequence: the per-call read is genuinely live, but nothing re-invokes injectHighlightStyles() when the OS setting flips, so a user switching their OS to dark mode (or enabling increased contrast, or reduced motion) mid-session keeps the previously injected CSS until some unrelated event happens to trigger a re-inject. l6m.28 fixed the resolution bug and its test proves the live read works when the function IS called; this bead covers making it get called. Fix: attach change listeners to the three media queries and re-run injectHighlightStyles() on fire. Note oculist-l6m.17's contrast gate has the same exposure, so this affects the dim treatment too. Done: flipping the OS colour scheme, contrast preference, or reduced-motion preference mid-session updates the injected CSS without any other user action; a test emulates each flip and asserts the CSS changes.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CLOSED via commit da4e589. Two of the three named flips got change listeners; the third is a proven no-op, not an omission. IMPLEMENTED: prefersMoreContrastQuery and reducedMotionQuery were already module-level singletons; prefers-color-scheme was not (getActiveThemeName called window.matchMedia fresh per invocation, so there was nothing to attach to), so a module-level colorSchemeQuery singleton was introduced and getActiveThemeName now reads colorSchemeQuery.matches. One addEventListener('change') per singleton re-runs injectHighlightStyles(). REDUCED-MOTION IS A NO-OP BY CONSTRUCTION, verified empirically rather than by reading: a probe snapshotted both injected stylesheets, flipped reducedMotion to reduce, and re-snapshotted with nothing else done. #oc-global-highlight-styles was byte-identical and contains no token matching /motion|prefers-reduced/i at all; #oc-dialog-styles was byte-identical with 'oc-no-motion' appearing exactly twice before and after (one static rule at content.js:5464-5468, emitted unconditionally). A listener would be a literal no-op re-inject and a CSS-diff test would have nothing to diff. The done-criteria's literal 'the CSS changes' wording is UNSATISFIABLE for this flip, not unimplemented. The bead's INTENT is satisfied: behaviour does update live, probed at 23 beacon parts on full motion, 0 after the flip, 23 restored, because effectiveMotion() (content.js:2180-2184) reads reducedMotionQuery.matches fresh per render, so there is no staleness window. That is already covered by test/prefers_reduced_motion.test.js:93. VERIFIED: retained MediaQueryList.matches confirmed live in-page; registration cannot stack (module scope, behind the top-of-file re-injection guard at content.js:4) and cannot fire before boot() (a change event cannot interrupt the synchronous IIFE); post-destroy flips throw nothing and leave exactly 1 global style element, and that element is present on every page at HEAD anyway; 15 alternating flips produced no style stacking. Suite 118 pass / 0 fail, no new waitForTimeout so oculist-l6m.32 is not regressed. KNOWN RESIDUE, deliberate: the listeners are not removed in __ocDestroy() (content.js:663), matching the existing chrome.storage.onChanged pattern, so a torn-down instance keeps re-injecting an inert style element on every OS flip for the page's lifetime.

title: Flaky: lite_mode_restore.test.js draft-ownership assertion fails intermittently under full-suite load
description: Found during oculist-l6m.42 review. One uncontrolled full-suite run hit AssertionError: 'the draft must own oculist-match while it is non-empty' at test/lite_mode_restore.test.js:225. Not seen in 10 subsequent controlled runs (5 on the working tree, 5 at detached HEAD), so it is rarer than oculist-nw4's resize flake. Recorded so the suite's flakiness is known to extend beyond the resize test rather than being written off as a single bad test. Same family as oculist-nw4 and oculist-l6m.32: readiness and wall-clock dependence under parallel load. Needs a repeat-run harness to characterise before fixing.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: LEFT OPEN deliberately after the oculist-l6m.32 conversion (commit e97e029). The implementer reported this bead as 'addressed as part of the general lite_mode_restore.test.js conversion', with no repro attempted since it was already rare. The reviewer judged that honest but not evidence: nothing in that diff targets this flake specifically and no test demonstrates it is gone. Closing would be closing on faith. The general conversion did replace lite_mode_restore.test.js's fixed waits with debounce-result polling, so this may well be fixed - it just is not shown. NEXT STEP: run the suite repeatedly on an idle machine (this flake was seen once in ~16 full runs, so it needs a repeat-run harness to characterise) and close only if it does not reappear. Related: oculist-nw4 and oculist-mmm were both closed by that same commit with verified root-cause fixes.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CLOSED on differential evidence, no code change required - this bead was resolved by oculist-l6m.32's sleep-to-poll conversion (commit e97e029). MECHANISM: the assertion moved to test/lite_mode_restore.test.js:358. Before the conversion, typeDraft() was fill() plus a fixed waitForTimeout(400) against a 400ms debounce plus a rescan, i.e. zero margin, then the test read CSS.highlights.get('oculist-match') once and asserted. That is exactly the described flake. Now the assertion is preceded by waitForContentScriptValue polling the SAME expression with the SAME predicate the assertion checks, at 30ms intervals with a 5000ms budget, so the value asserted on is by construction one that satisfies the predicate. The named AssertionError is structurally unreachable; the only reachable failure is a poll timeout, which raises a different, self-describing error. POSITIVE CONTROL, which is what actually closes this: the reviewer restored the pre-conversion file as a temp probe and ran both versions under 12 CPU burners at load average ~45. OLD version, 8 runs: 1 FAIL with the bead's exact symptom, reproduced verbatim on demand. CURRENT version, 14 runs under identical load: 14/14 pass. The load condition demonstrably reproduces the flake on old code and not on new, which is a differential rather than an absence of evidence. Corroboration: 62 total runs of the current code across orchestrator and reviewer, zero reproductions. NOTED STRICTNESS LOSS, not a blocker: the old test asserted ownership was correct at T+400ms; the new one asserts it becomes correct within 5s. A regression that merely DELAYS draft ownership by up to 5s would now pass. That is correct semantics for a debounced pipeline, but the invariant is enforced by the poll's timeout rather than by the assert line, which is a tautology of the poll.

title: Two fixed 300ms sleeps in active_match_magnifier.test.js are unprincipled and under-sized
description: Found during oculist-l6m.42 review. The two tests added for l6m.42 use page.waitForTimeout(300) at test/active_match_magnifier.test.js:566 and :620 to settle a race before toggling settings. The implementer added them to fix a reported false-negative negative control, but the reviewer could not reproduce that false negative: reducing the settle wait to 0ms still produced a clean negative-control failure 3/3. Worse, the scroll path defers up to 600ms (content.js:3269), so 300ms does not even cover the branch these tests take. The waits are 'usually-green' rather than principled. Fix: replace both with a condition-based wait on the actual readiness signal. The underlying production race (a deferred animate() at content.js:3293 reading settings at fire time, so a late animate can draw the card on its own) is benign and not worth its own bead - a setting applying a few ms early is not user-visible. Fold into oculist-l6m.32 if that bead is taken first.

title: Flaky: 'repositions on resize' test in active_match_magnifier.test.js intermittently fails under full-suite load
description: During full 'npm test' runs (not isolated), test/active_match_magnifier.test.js's 'repositions on resize instead of stranding in old document coordinates' test intermittently fails with 'card should start centered on the match, dx=-476...ms' — a large offset suggesting the 100ms resize debounce/reflow hadn't settled within the 5000ms waitForFunction window under full-suite CPU contention. Reproduced on 2 of 4 full-suite runs (2026-08-26); passes reliably in isolation (node --test test/active_match_magnifier.test.js). Unrelated to oculist-l6m.42's fix — observed both before and after that change. Likely needs a more generous timeout or a more robust readiness check than the current dx<6 poll.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CORRECTION - the diagnosis in this bead's description is wrong and will send an implementer to the wrong line. Established during the oculist-l6m.42 review with 10 controlled full-suite runs (5 on the working tree, 5 on a detached HEAD worktree; the resize test failed 0/5 in BOTH, so the flake did not reproduce under controlled conditions at all). The failing assertion is assert.ok(Math.abs(before.dx) < 6, ...) at test/active_match_magnifier.test.js:415, which runs BEFORE any resize happens - so the cause is not an unsettled 100ms resize debounce. The real cause: the readiness gate searchUntilMagnifierWord() polls only the card's TEXT and never its POSITION, so the test proceeds while the card is still at stale coordinates. Fix direction: make the readiness gate assert on position as well as text. Also NOT the same root cause as oculist-l6m.32 - this test uses waitForFunction throughout rather than fixed sleeps, so l6m.32's '106 fixed sleeps' framing does not cover it, though both are the same family of readiness/wall-clock dependence.

title: loadWorkList mount restore writes workListTerms/activeTermIndex without a rescan, so the .20 invariant does not literally hold
description: Found during oculist-l6m.15 review. content.js:4550 (the loadWorkList mount-restore callback) is a 0-to-N workListTerms transition that does NOT call performListSearch() and does NOT reset termRanges - it calls renderChipRow() directly. It is safe today only by virtue of __ocDestroy (content.js:674) zeroing termRanges, and every reopen routing through it, so termRanges is provably [] at that point. Only a theoretical race could beat it (a chrome.storage.session callback losing to a 150ms input debounce plus a 350ms mutation debounce), which in-memory storage makes unreachable in practice. The issue is that the invariant comment landed by oculist-l6m.20 at content.js:2521 states 'every writer of activeTermIndex must call performListSearch() synchronously after setting it', and this call site does not do that. Either route this site through the rescan, or amend the comment to name the __ocDestroy-zeroing exception explicitly. Leaving it as-is means the documented invariant is subtly false, which is the exact failure mode .20 was closed to avoid.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: STOPPED after two failed reviews, left IN_PROGRESS with work UNCOMMITTED on branch epic/oculist-followups. The production change PASSED both reviews and is correct; the test file is what failed, twice, in the same way. PRODUCTION (good, verified twice, content.js SHA-256 020be66f...dccb06 byte-identical across both reviews): content.js:4670 sets termRanges = [] explicitly in the loadWorkList mount-restore callback, making the site locally correct rather than dependent on __ocDestroy zeroing it. The oculist-l6m.20 invariant comment at content.js:2620-2628 was amended to allow two legal forms, and the reviewer verified it is now literally true of all 9 activeTermIndex write sites: :646 init and :742 __ocDestroy and :4194 loadSavedList and :4666 mount-restore all satisfy form 2 (set termRanges consistently), while :3080 activateChip and :3098/:3100/:3102 removeChipAt and :3187 addChipTerm satisfy form 1 (synchronous performListSearch). No writer satisfies neither. REVIEW 1 FAILURE: the no-scan assertion was decorative - injecting a real buildPageIndex() into the restore path left the suite green, because the getComputedStyle baseline was captured after the restore had already completed. Fixed in the second pass via installRestoreProbe(), which brackets the callback synchronously inside a patched chrome.storage.session.get; the reviewer reproduced that injecting buildPageIndex() now correctly fails with 3 !== 2. That part is genuinely fixed. REVIEW 2 FAILURE, still outstanding: the out-of-range test's NAME and comment claim it pins normalizeWorkList's clamp, and the describe header repeats the claim. It does not. The reviewer deleted the clamp at content.js:108 and the suite stayed 5/5 green, proving the mutation was live with a peek hook showing activeTermIndex = 99 at the callback. The test stays green only because of renderChipRow's tolerance (isActive = i === activeTermIndex never matching), which the comment explicitly disclaims as not being what it tests. Both halves of the comment are backwards, and the previous vaguer name was net better than the new specific-but-wrong one. TO FINISH: either assert the observed index is -1 (a value-level assertion that diverges at 99), or strip the mechanism claim from the test name, its comment, and describe-header claim (3), describing it as what it is - an end-to-end no-throw/no-active-chip render check that does not distinguish sanitizer from renderer. Nit: the comment cites normalizeWorkList at content.js:102-109; it is actually at 103-110. NOTE THE PATTERN worth human attention: on a bead whose entire subject is documentation promising what the code does not enforce, the implementer shipped exactly that defect twice.

title: Toggling a vision setting does not redraw the current match
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.39 review. Pre-existing, shared by magnifier and textLabels.

The chrome.storage.onChanged listener (content.js:5355-5360) does not call
repositionActiveOverlays(), so flipping Match Labels or the new Magnifier toggle does not swap
the overlay in or out on the match currently on screen. The change only appears on the next
navigation or redraw.

A user toggling the setting to see what it does gets no feedback and reasonably concludes it is
broken.

Done: a vision-settings change redraws the active match's overlays in place; a test toggles the
magnifier with a match on screen and asserts the card appears without navigating.

title: Nothing tests the magnifier's font scaling or truncation
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.39 review. The code is correct (the reviewer verified it at
content.js:1975-1979) but no test protects it.

Untested:
- font-size derived from the MATCH's own computed font-size x 2.5, clamped to 16-48px. This was
  called out in the bead as the point most likely to be got wrong, precisely because bead .11
  records the same mistake being made with getBeaconScale() for chip sizing. A regression here
  would be silent.
- the ~24-character truncation with ellipsis for long matches.

Also minor, same file: test/active_match_magnifier.test.js shares one browser page across the
whole file, so one failure cascades into later tests. Harmless while green, noisier when red.

Done: tests pin the x2.5 derivation, both clamp bounds, and the truncation; the suite isolates
its page per test or resets state between them.

title: Chip accessible-name tests assert the raw attribute and skip two states
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.16 review. The behaviour is correct (the reviewer verified it live via
the CDP accessibility tree), but the committed tests are weaker than the verification was.

1. test/chip_count_accessibility.test.js:145 and :156 assert getAttribute('aria-label'), the raw
   attribute, rather than the computed accessible name. Those differ whenever name computation
   changes precedence, which is exactly the kind of regression this test exists to catch.
2. No test covers the two subtle states: a cap-starved chip (skipped because the total match cap
   was hit, lands in the sparse-array undefined bucket and must announce no count) and a Lite Mode
   chip (announces the real count from countMatchesOnly). Both were verified by hand only, so a
   regression in either would go unnoticed.

Done: the assertions read the computed accessible name, and both the cap-starved and Lite Mode
states have coverage.

title: restoreActiveChip claims 'no match' for an unscanned chip via the input debounce
description:
Found during the oculist-l6m.19 re-review. Same false-claim class as the regression .19 fixed,
reached through a different entry point, so .19's guard does not cover it.

restoreActiveChip (content.js:2499-2501) writes i18n.noMatch for an unscanned chip when
reached via the INPUT DEBOUNCE rather than via findNext. Repro: against a restored but
unscanned working list, type a draft then clear the input. The debounce fires,
restoreActiveChip runs, and the count reads "no match" for a chip whose term may well have
matches on the page, because it has never been scanned.

Count and nav still agree (nav disabled, nothing highlighted), so this is cosmetic, but it is
the extension stating something false about the page.

The distinction .19 established is the fix: termRanges[i] === undefined means never scanned
(show blank), an empty array means scanned with genuinely zero matches (show "no match").
Apply the same test here.

Done: an unscanned chip restored via the debounce path shows a blank count, not "no match";
a test covers type-then-clear against a restored unscanned list.

title: welcome.js localStorage fallback contradicts the privacy policy
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.10 review. Low severity, pre-existing.

extension/welcome.js:665,672 read and write localStorage['oc-settings'], which contradicts
PRIVACY.md's statement that Oculist writes to no storage area other than the ones listed.

It is a dead fallback branch: chrome.storage.sync is always defined on an extension page, so
no user data actually lands in localStorage. But the policy sentence is absolute and the code
is not.

Done: delete the dead branch, or soften the policy sentence to match. Deleting is preferable,
since an absolute privacy claim is worth more than an unreachable fallback.

title: loadSavedList does not clear the pending search debounce
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.9 review.

loadSavedList (content.js:3615) does not clearTimeout(debounceTimer). Typing a draft and then
loading a list inside the 150ms debounce window lets the debounce fire afterwards with
input.value === '', reaching restoreActiveChip() -> performSearch('') with
activeTermIndex === -1.

Benign today (it clears to the empty state) but it is an unintended scan-adjacent call on a
path whose whole contract is "loading runs no scan".

Done: loadSavedList clears the pending debounce; a test loads a list mid-debounce.

title: Theme hover colour reads settings.theme instead of the resolved theme
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.9 review. Three sites, same mistake, fix together.

content.js:4888 (new, from .9), :4303 and :4741 (both pre-existing) use
settings.theme === 'dark' rather than the already-in-scope resolved activeTheme (:4176).
Under theme 'system' with a dark OS, the hover tint renders the light-mode value.

Done: all three use the resolved theme; a test covers system-theme + dark OS.

title: Saved-list storage rough edges
description:
Three minor findings from the oculist-l6m.8 review.

1. deleteList (content.js:378) reuses the SAVE failure message on a delete failure, so a
   failed delete tells the user "delete a saved list and try again". Needs its own string.
2. readListIndex (content.js:272-277) counts junk keys toward the 50-list cap, while
   listSavedLists hides them. A corrupted oc-list-* key could block saving while the user
   sees fewer than 50 lists and cannot work out why.
3. Note only, not fixable with the chrome.storage API: an inherent TOCTOU between the cap
   read (content.js:304) and the write (content.js:314) means two devices sitting at 49
   lists can both pass the check.

Done: 1 and 2 fixed, 3 recorded as a comment where the race lives.

title: Saved-list storage: three untested branches
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.8 review. The behaviour is correct (the reviewer verified all three
by hand via a CDP probe) but the suite does not cover them, so a regression would ship silently.

1. generateListId's collision loop (content.js:217-226) has ZERO coverage. The existing
   assertion notStrictEqual(second.list.id, first.list.id) passes even if the function
   ignored existingIds entirely.
2. The 10-term and 100-char caps in sanitizeListTerms are untested, despite being a stated
   done-criterion of .8. Verified by hand: 16 terms in -> 10 out, 150-char term -> exactly 100.
3. The 50-list cap test catches a permissive off-by-one (> vs >=) but not an over-strict one,
   because no test saves the 50th list successfully.

Done: each of the three has a test that fails against the corresponding wrong implementation.

title: Consolidate the six window.__oc* test-only hooks
description:
Do this AFTER oculist-l6m.9, so the UI tests exist and can make some hooks redundant.

There are now six test-reachability hooks on the isolated-world window: __ocLoadWorkList and
__ocSaveWorkList from .2, plus __ocSaveList, __ocListSavedLists, __ocRenameList, and
__ocDeleteList from .8. Plus the pre-existing __ocToggle and __ocDestroy, which are a real
call path and stay.

Two reviews have now confirmed empirically that these land in the extension's isolated world
and are undefined in the host page, so this is not a security issue. It is accumulating
production surface that exists only for tests, and .2's review already warned against growing it.

The hooks were genuinely necessary: they are IIFE closures, CDP Runtime.evaluate only reaches
globals, and testing through chrome.storage directly would test Chrome's API rather than this
code.

Done: the six test-only hooks are collapsed into a single window.__ocTest namespace, or
deleted where .9's UI tests reach the same behaviour through the interface.

title: Match-cap feedback is misleading in two ways
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.7 review. Both are user-facing copy/affordance problems, not logic
errors.

1. The notice reads "Showing the first 2000 matches. Remove a term for a complete count."
   but the cap is checked BEFORE materialising each term, so the real total can reach 2997.
   The new cap test documents this. The number in the message is simply not true. This
   string came from the v1.7.0 design doc, so the spec is the source of the error.
   Fix direction: say "Showing about the first 2000 matches" or check the cap after
   materialising and report the real figure.

2. A starved chip (skipped because the cap was hit) renders a BLANK count, which is visually
   identical to "not scanned yet" (content.js:2591). The cap notice mitigates this globally
   but the two per-chip states are indistinguishable, so the user cannot tell which terms
   were actually skipped.
   Fix direction: render a distinct marker on starved chips.

Done: the notice states a number that matches reality, and a starved chip is visually
distinct from an unscanned one.

title: traverse() duplicates a narrower check instead of using isOculistNode()
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.4 review.

The self-match fix added an identity check `child !== wrap` to traverse(). It is sufficient
today, because traverse() starts at document.body and every beacon, marker, and label is
mounted on document.documentElement, while oc-global-highlight-styles is a <style> already
covered by SKIP_TAGS.

But it is a partial duplicate of the existing isOculistNode() helper and will silently miss
any future Oculist-owned node mounted under body. The next person to add one gets phantom
matches with no failing test.

Done: traverse() routes through isOculistNode(), or the identity check carries a comment
explaining why it deliberately does not.

title: Chip sizing keys off getBeaconScale(), the beacon knob
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.3 review.

Chip text size is derived from getBeaconScale() (the vision-profile beacon size s/m/l/xl).
At xl (2.25) chip text renders at 27px. That is the only scale hook in content.js, but it
is the BEACON knob, not a UI-text knob, so chip sizing is riding on an unrelated setting.

Needs a design decision: either introduce a separate UI-text scale, or clamp the chip
scale, or accept the coupling deliberately and comment it.

Done: chips render at a sensible size across all four beacon sizes, and whichever way it
is resolved is recorded in a comment.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: RESOLUTION: clamped, not a separate UI-text scale. getChipScale() (content.js:487-494) clamps getBeaconScale() to [1, 1.5] for chip use; the 10 real beacon call sites keep the full 0.7-2.25 range. Chip text is therefore 12px at s/m and 18px at l/xl, down from 8.4px/27px at the extremes. Rejected a separate UI-text scale as a new setting + UI + persistence + migration for a cosmetic issue. Pinned by a test in test/chip_row.test.js asserting computed font-size across all four beacon sizes; mutation-verified to fail at both ends.

title: Release chores for v1.7.0
description:
Steps:
1. Bump repo/extension/manifest.json version to 1.7.0.
2. Add a 1.7.0 entry to repo/CHANGELOG.md describing multi-term lists, saved lists, and the
   carry-over behaviour.
3. Confirm no new manifest permissions were added. 'storage' was already granted, so there
   is no new Chrome Web Store permission justification to write. If a permission did creep

BLOCKING ADDITION from the .9 review — PRIVACY.md is now factually wrong and this is a Chrome Web Store disclosure issue, not a docs nit.

this epic and are unrelated to it. Do not sweep them into your commit. Report what you find

title: No regression guard on the popup version badge
description:
Reviewer finding from oculist-6iu. The popup version badge is now sourced from chrome.runtime.getManifest().version (extension/popup.js:4-7) into <span id='version-text'> (extension/popup.html:473), but NO test asserts on it. description:

title: Regression test for the stale-mount loadWorkList guard
description: The oculist-3z6 mountGeneration guard in extension/content.js (buildUI's loadWorkList callback) is verified only by an injected-delay probe script, not by any committed test - a revert would go unnoticed until the load flake returns. Add a deterministic regression test using the delay-injection pattern from the reviewer's probe (delay only the first mount's storage.session.get callback, teardown, seed oc-worklist, remount, assert the chip row survives and the stale callback did not clobber it). The reviewer's working method is recorded in the oculist-3z6 comments; scratchpad/repro_3z6.js had the exact steps.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Landed test/stale_mount_guard.test.js: one-shot delay injection on chrome.storage.session.get defers only mount A's loadWorkList callback; mount B restores a seeded list; the test asserts the chip survives the stale callback. Reviewer ran the guard-revert mutation independently: red with the clobber message, green restored. Reviewer notes for the record: the wrapper issues the read immediately and defers only callback delivery (so mount A captures the pre-seed state - load-bearing design); the residual race direction is safe (a >3s mount B would false-PASS under mutation, never false-FAIL, ~50x measured margin); installDelayOnNextGet would not re-arm if called twice (footgun if the file grows).

description: From the oculist-fvc review. box_sizing_defense.test.js:173, chip_row.test.js:111, list_menu.test.js:110, and spa_navigation.test.js:73 carry the same intentional bare timeout:250 sub-poll (20-attempt loop + scaled POLL_TIMEOUT backstop) that oculist-fvc just documented in dispersion_bloom.test.js. title: Enumeration orphan parser misreports appended prose as an orphan label
description:
From the oculist-5v9 review. The orphan detection in test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js bounds prose slices at

, so an ordinary sentence appended inside the same

after the effect list (e.g. '...and Cyber-Vision. All are GPU-friendly.') is parsed as a bogus orphan label and fails with a misleading 'stale/orphaned label' diagnosis. Same for a lead-in clause added before the docs intro list. Failure is loud and quotes the text, so debuggable, but the message misdiagnoses. FIX: bound the prose slices at the sentence boundary (the period ending the list) rather than

, or make the orphan message distinguish 'unparseable trailing text' from a genuine stale label.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Closed with option (a): welcome prose orphan slice ends at the first period after the list start (loud-failing fallback if absent); docs intro orphan slice starts at the first registry label instead of the p tag (can only widen, so mis-slice direction is false-positive, never concealment). All four mutation classes re-verified red by the reviewer. Accepted residuals: (1) a lead-in that itself contains the first label still gets the misleading orphan diagnosis (safe direction); (2) a stale label relocated into trailing prose after the sentence period would be missed by the orphan check, though assertLabelsInOrder and the count test still catch genuine removals; (3) the docs slice's safety depends on assertLabelsInOrder running before the orphan check - statement order matters, noted in a comment.

title: Lightning async second phase has no cancel-regression test
description: From the oculist-kqv review. animateLightning schedules its flash/flicker second phase via setTimeout(travelDuration~350ms); an isConnected guard (extension/content.js:~1885) stops it from creating animations on a cancelled container. The waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js lightning subtest snapshots before cancel and asserts immediately after, so removing the guard would still pass. FIX: extend that subtest to cancel early, wait past travelDuration, then assert document.getAnimations() holds no running beacon animations. The reviewer verified the behavior manually with a Playwright probe; this bead just locks it into the suite.

title: Light Cycle MIN_SEG_SEP guard is a no-op when midYVp is pinned at the viewport bound
description: Found by the oculist-dvt.8 reviewer. The MIN_SEG_SEP=12 guard (extension/content.js:2502-2507) re-clamps its downward push to window.innerHeight - 26, which is exactly the bound that produced the degeneracy, so for a match low in the viewport the push is a no-op: brute-force over vpCy 0-800 x mh 8-200 at innerHeight=800 found 1848 configurations still under 12px separation, 231 under 1.5px, including exact zero (vpCy=678, mh=160 gives mid = fin = 774, a 1px stub via Math.max(len,1)). The guard is safe (never inverts or leaves the viewport) but incomplete, and the comment at content.js:2496-2501 overstates it. FIX: when the downward push is blocked by the viewport bound, fall back to midYVp = finalYVp - MIN_SEG_SEP. Add a test that exercises a degenerate low-match geometry; nothing covers the guard today.

title: Enumeration sync test: scope welcome.html scan and cover removals
description: Follow-ups from the oculist-dvt.10 review. (1) extension/welcome.html:291-297 holds a FOURTH unsynced effect enumeration (settings-panel mockup <option> list) not covered by test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js. (2) The welcome.html scan is unscoped (whole file), so a label deleted from the line-226 prose is misreported as a different missing label; scope the slice to the prose paragraph. comments.author: ya8282
