title: Effect-list overflow test hardcodes a registry count of 13
description:
Two nits from the oculist-dvt.5 reviewer, both cosmetic, filed so they are not lost.

1. test/settings_panel_effect_list_overflow.test.js:200, :230 and :304 each re-assert keys.length === 13, duplicating what test 1 already does. The reviewer's 16-effect mutation produced 'pass 1 / fail 4': the scroll-container property genuinely still held (scrollHeight 414 > clientHeight 220, so the fix works at 16), but four hardcoded count assertions failed loudly with messages saying 'expected 13 rows' rather than naming a reachability problem. Adding a 14th effect will therefore produce four noisy misleading failures instead of one honest registry-count failure. FIX: assert the count once, and have the other three tests derive the expected count from the registry rather than hardcoding it.

2. Only ONE of the five tests actually detects the fix's absence - the scrollHeight > clientHeight assertion. The other four pass under a full CSS revert because at the default vh=800 the uncapped 790.4px panel still fits by 9.6px. That single assertion is the whole guard. Consider pinning host height against a baseline, or running one of the tests at a shorter viewport where the uncapped panel genuinely clips, so the guard does not rest on one proxy.

DONE: adding a 14th effect fails at most one test, with a message that names the real problem; and more than one test detects a full revert of the CSS fix.

title: Speed Lines lane assertion cannot catch whole-effect mispositioning
description: Found by the oculist-dvt.1 re-reviewer via an adversarial mutation the fix was not designed for. The clear-lane test now pins that the lane brackets the match (window.__ocTest.lastSpeedLinesLaneBounds) and that it attenuates real streaks, which kills every fake-lane mutation. BUT mutating the shared anchor itself - 'var offsetY = my - targetTop + 200' at extension/content.js:2078 - survives 4/4 green. offsetY is the single anchor for the streak y positions (:2123), the flare gradient (:2241, :2246), the hot core (:2250) and transformOrigin (:2090), so lane, streaks and flare all translate together: the bracket assertion still holds while the entire beacon fires 200px below the word. This is whole-effect mispositioning, a DIFFERENT failure mode from the fake-clear-lane gap the bead was failed on - the lane still does its job relative to the field it clears - which is why it did not block the bead. FIX: anchor the assertion outside the implementation, e.g. compare the reported matchY against the target element's own getBoundingClientRect() mapped into container-local coordinates, so the test has an independent source of truth for where the match actually is. NOTE this likely applies to the other three effects in this epic too - consider a shared positional assertion helper once Chrono Tunnel, Light Cycle and Cyber-Vision have landed, rather than four bespoke ones. DONE: shifting offsetY by 200px fails a test.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: WIDEN THIS BEAD to cover canvas effects generally, not just Speed Lines. The oculist-dvt.2 reviewer confirmed Chrono Tunnel has the identical gap: offsetting the ring centre by 150px (extension/content.js:2408-2409) leaves all 5 chrono tests green, because the rings, the wobble and the core glow all translate together against the same anchor. Same root cause as the Speed Lines offsetY finding - the assertions are anchored inside the implementation, so whole-effect mispositioning is invisible. Expect the same for Light Cycle and Cyber-Vision. FIX: one shared positional helper that maps the target element's own getBoundingClientRect() into container-local coordinates and asserts the effect's anchor against it, used by all four effect suites, rather than four bespoke assertions. SEPARATE MINOR ITEM from the same review: chrono's core glow hue (content.js:2419) is not pinned - swapping it to a fixed spectrum leaves 5/5 green because coreHue is never pushed into hueSamples. The shipped code correctly calls hueAt(0,t), so this is coverage, not a defect; one extra hueSamples.push(coreHue) closes it.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Closed with a shared helper test/helpers/effect_anchor.js (elementCenterInContainer) used by speed_lines and chrono_tunnel via new lastSpeedLinesAnchor/lastChronoAnchor hooks; light_cycle asserts its real DOM box against the match rect (BOX_BORDER=2 correction, analytically justified); cyber_vision already anchored externally, untouched. coreHue now enters hueSamples so a fixed-spectrum core-glow mutation fails. All five mispositioning/hue mutations verified caught by the reviewer. Known limit, documented in the helper header: helper is only valid at getBeaconScale()===1; a future beaconSize-sweeping caller would get silently wrong numbers.

title: generateListId collision test can leak a frozen Date.now/Math.random
description: Found by the oculist-l6m.22 reviewer. The collision test at test/list_storage.test.js:329-334 freezes Date.now and Math.random in the content-script context, then restores them only INSIDE the saveList callback. If that callback never fires (a rejected write, a thrown error, a timeout), the frozen clock and RNG leak into every remaining test in the file. Two consequences: (1) later tests in list_storage.test.js could behave nondeterministically after an unrelated failure, making the first failure's cause hard to read; (2) separately, if any unrelated page code consumed Math.random between the freeze and generateListId, the test would go green VACUOUSLY rather than fail - a false-negative path. Not observed across 18+ runs, so this is robustness, not a live defect. FIX: restore the overrides in a finally-style guard that runs whether or not the callback fires, and assert the id actually consumed the frozen values so a vacuous pass surfaces as a failure. DONE: forcing saveList's callback never to fire leaves Date.now and Math.random restored for subsequent tests.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Closed with the finally-backstopped restore (window.__ocFreezeState + idempotent restore reissued from node-side finally, withTimeout bounding a stuck saveList callback) and two anti-vacuity assertions (id embeds frozen Date.now base36; callCountBeforeSave===0 discriminates pre-generateListId burns). Reviewer-verified by three sabotage runs. Accepted residuals, recorded not fixed: (1) a Math.random burn INSIDE content.js's saveList->readListIndex path (after the snapshot) would still pass vacuously - closable later by counting frozen Date.now calls per attempt; (2) __ocFreezeState is never deleted and an unreachable double-freeze would stash frozen fns as originals; (3) the finally's restore eval is itself unbounded and could mask the original error if it rejected. All judged diminishing-returns for a test-robustness bead.

title: test/dispersion_bloom.test.js:164 has a bare timeout: 250
description: Left over from the oculist-rdx sweep, spotted by the oculist-12f reviewer. Most bare 'timeout: 250' values in test/ are per-attempt sub-polls inside 20-attempt retry loops backed by a following scaled page.waitForSelector, which is why oculist-rdx deliberately left them unscaled. Verify whether the one at test/dispersion_bloom.test.js:164 fits that pattern or is a standalone budget that should derive from POLL_TIMEOUT. DONE: the literal is either routed through the shared constants or carries a comment naming it as an intentional short sub-poll.

title: Bloom full-mode assertions live under a Lite Mode test name
description: Found by the oculist-12f reviewer. The full-mode ring offset-order and offset/end-scale pairing assertions added by oculist-12f sit inside the test titled 'Lite Mode drops the ring count from 3 to 1...' in test/dispersion_bloom.test.js (~line 400), because that test already had the full-mode-vs-lite-mode comparison set up. A full-mode pairing regression therefore reports under a Lite Mode test name, which will mislead whoever reads the failure. Structural and pre-existing - oculist-12f extended the existing test rather than introducing the mismatch. FIX: split the full-mode offset/scale contract into its own test block with an accurate name, reusing the ringHueOffsets()/ringEndScales() helpers. DONE: a full-mode pairing mutation fails a test whose name names full mode.

title: Stale synced settings.effect never self-heals in storage
description: Found by the oculist-7z3 reviewer. The registry guard added at content.js:6074 normalises settings.effect in memory but does not call saveSettings(), so chrome.storage.sync keeps the invalid value (e.g. 'lens' from a device on an old build). Every subsequent onChanged echo therefore re-compares 'lens' !== 'hud', sets changed = true, and triggers a full rebuildSettingsPanelPreservingFocus() - permanent low-grade churn for any user with a stale synced value, until they click an effect option and saveSettings() overwrites it. Consistent with the boot-time guard at content.js:6123, which also does not write back, so this is pre-existing behaviour that oculist-7z3 extended rather than introduced. FIX (if judged worth it): have the guard write the normalised value back, or suppress the redraw when the only changed key was normalised to its prior value. Weigh against the risk of a write loop between two devices disagreeing on the effect set. DONE: a stale stored effect is either repaired in storage once, or demonstrably stops triggering repeat rebuilds.

title: storage.onChanged applies settings.effect with no registry guard
description: Found during the oculist-e9u (Lens removal) review. The chrome.storage.onChanged listener at extension/content.js:6062-6069 iterates SETTINGS_KEYS and does settings[k] = nv[k] unconditionally, including 'effect'. It does NOT re-run the boot-time validity guard at content.js:6122 (if (!effectsRegistry[settings.effect]) settings.effect = 'hud'), which only executes inside the initial chrome.storage.sync.get callback. So a remote or stale sync write naming a removed effect - e.g. 'lens' from a device still on the old build - lands in settings.effect post-boot with nothing normalising it. NOT a functional break: animate()'s own fallback (content.js:2589, effectsRegistry[effectKey] || effectsRegistry.hud) catches it at render time and a working HUD beacon still fires; this is pinned by the oculist-e9u regression test in test/settings_panel.test.js, which drives exactly this path. The visible symptom is cosmetic and confined to the settings panel: the effect picker is makeRadioList (content.js:4062-4103), which marks a row active only on an exact item.value === currentVal match, so an unrecognised value matches nothing and EVERY row renders an empty dot - the panel shows no selection at all while the beacon actually renders HUD. It self-heals as soon as the user clicks any option (saveSettings). FIX: apply the same registry guard in the onChanged path, so settings.effect is normalised wherever it is written, not only at boot. DONE: a post-boot storage change naming an unknown effect leaves settings.effect as 'hud' and the panel shows hud selected.

title: Lens: the 1200px source height cap is covered by no test
description: Inverse of oculist-wwu, found by the same reviewer with the opposite mutation. wwu made animateLens's body/html bail independently provable via a short-body fixture. Running the mutation the other way - deleting BOTH height caps (extension/content.js:1666 and the in-walk 'candRect.height <= 1200' at :1641) while leaving the bail intact - leaves the FULL suite green at 145/145. So the cap is now the unproven guard: nothing anywhere fails if it is removed or broken. FIX: add a fixture where the match's nearest non-inline ancestor is a real element (NOT body) taller than 1200px, so the bail cannot fire and the cap is the only guard in play. Assert the lens falls back to the match's immediate parent rather than cloning the oversized ancestor. DONE: deleting the 1200px cap alone fails a test. RELATED NOTE from the same review: the wwu test's 'lens did not mount' branch passes vacuously if the lens fails to draw for an unrelated reason (finder not focused, Enter swallowed). Not vacuous today - mutation proves it bites - and a contention flake would surface as a false failure rather than a false pass, so this is a robustness note, not a correctness bug.

title: Bloom: nothing asserts ring end scales or DOM order
description: Found during the oculist-4qt review by mutation probe. Reversing BOTH ringHueOffsets and ringEndScales in animateDispersion's full-mode path (so -22 pairs with end scale 24.5 instead of 18) leaves the entire suite GREEN, 4/4. Two blind spots cause it: (1) test/dispersion_bloom.test.js:373 sorts the offsets before comparing, so ring DOM order is invisible to the assertion; (2) assertColorsMatch is documented as order-independent; and (3) nothing anywhere in test/ asserts the end-scale values 18/21/24.5 at all. So the 'three rings at -22/0/+22 with end scales 18/21/24.5, in that order' contract is verified only by reading the code. The Lite Mode case is the exception - its offset-0/scale-21 pairing is structurally guaranteed by the shared centred slice, so it needs no separate pinning. FIX: assert the end scales (readable from each ring's animation keyframes or a data attribute if one is added), and compare offsets in DOM order rather than sorted. DONE: reversing the offset/scale arrays, or mispairing an offset with the wrong end scale, fails a test. SEPARATE MINOR ITEM from the same review: for ringCount > 3 the centred-slice arithmetic yields a negative ringStart, so slice(-1, 3) silently under-renders (ringCount 4 or 5 draws ONE ring, not four). No undefined or NaN, so it is safe, but quietly wrong. Clamp with Math.max(0, ringStart) or add a comment naming the ceiling, if ringCount ever becomes tunable.

title: Lens: the body/html bail and the 1200px source cap mask each other in tests
description: In animateLens (extension/content.js ~1600), two guards stop the effect cloning the whole document: an unconditional bail when the resolved sourceEl is document.body/documentElement, and a ~1200px height cap on the resolved source. In test/lens_effect.test.js the fixture body is ~2000px tall, so removing the bail alone still leaves the suite green (the height cap catches it instead); only removing BOTH turns it red. The assertion is not vacuous, but the bail is not independently mutation-provable. FIX: add a fixture page with a SHORT body (under 1200px) carrying a bare text-node match directly under <body>, so the bail is the only guard in play and removing it goes red on its own. Found by the reviewer on oculist-y6a, ruled non-blocking. DONE: removing the body/html bail alone fails a test.

title: Dispersion Bloom's Lite Mode ring uses the -22 hue offset, not the base palette hue
description: In animateDispersion (extension/content.js:1381-1383), the ring loop indexes hueOffsets by r. With ringCount = 1 under Lite Mode (settings.performanceMode), the single rendered ring therefore takes hueOffsets[0] === -22 rather than the base 0 offset — so Lite Mode users see the beacon shifted 22 degrees off getEffectiveColors().beacon instead of the palette colour itself. Still palette-derived and still colourblind-safe, so this is cosmetic, not an accessibility defect. FIX: when ringCount === 1, emit the 0 offset (e.g. pick the middle of the offsets array, or slice the offsets to a centred subset sized to ringCount). Also add a length guard so endScales/hueOffsets indexing cannot silently yield undefined/NaN colours if ringCount ever grows past the array length — safe today only because it is always 1 or 3. Found by the reviewer on oculist-dvv, ruled non-blocking. DONE: Lite Mode renders one ring at the unshifted palette beacon hue, and a test pins it.

title: renameList silently discards a malformed terms value with no user notice
description: Found during oculist-dzi review. renameList (content.js:386) does terms: Array.isArray(existing.terms) ? existing.terms : [], so renaming an entry whose terms is malformed silently replaces it with an empty array. The user gets no notice that data was discarded. This path was unreachable before oculist-dzi, because malformed entries were invisible in the panel and so had no reachable rename button; dzi made them visible and deletable, which also made this the one user-reachable lossy path it opened up. dzi corrected the comment at content.js:363-366 so the behaviour is at least documented, which was the actual ask there, but the silence to the user remains. Normalising garbage on an explicit user write is defensible and matches the 0-terms badge the panel already shows, so this is low priority. Options: leave as-is now that it is documented; surface a notice via showNotice with its own key (the per-class notice machinery from oculist-l6m.12 makes this cheap); or preserve the unknown value so a user could recover it. Done: renaming an entry with malformed terms either tells the user the value was discarded, or preserves it.

title: traverse()'s text-node branch still duplicates isOculistNode() with an ad-hoc oc-beacon check
description: Found during oculist-l6m.14 review. content.js:2248 (the text-node branch of traverse()) still uses an ad-hoc parent.classList.contains('oc-beacon') instead of routing through isOculistNode(), which is the last remaining duplicate of that helper inside traverse() after l6m.14 fixed the element branch. It is currently dead defense rather than a live gap: any Oculist ancestor is now rejected before descent, so the text-node branch can no longer be reached for Oculist-owned text. Worth collapsing for the same reason l6m.14 existed - the duplicate will silently diverge from isOculistNode() if the helper gains a new marker. Done: the text-node branch routes through isOculistNode(), or carries a comment saying why it deliberately does not.

title: X-button chip removal briefly shows the removed term's count and highlights for one debounce tick
description: Found during oculist-l6m.33 review, verified with a live probe. Removing the only chip via the X button while a search debounce is still in flight (<150ms) shows the removed term's stale count and highlights for one debounce tick, then self-heals to the draft's correct state. Transient, self-limiting, and internally consistent throughout - the count, nav state and highlights agree with each other at every instant, they are just briefly the removed term's. Not a done-criteria failure for .33; filed as polish. Fix would be to cancel or invalidate the in-flight debounce on X-button removal the way the Backspace path already resets lastTerm (content.js removeChipAt, ~line 3003).

title: Whitespace-only stored terms render an enabled load control that does nothing
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.26 review. Corrupted or hand-edited storage only, non-destructive.

Three gates disagree about what counts as an empty term list:
- buildListItem (content.js:3753) gates on raw list.terms.length
- loadSavedList (content.js:3682) gates on sanitizeListTerms(...).length
- listSavedLists (content.js:250) filters to strings without trimming

So a stored list with terms: ['   '] renders an ENABLED load control badged "1 term", and
clicking it is a silent no-op, because loadSavedList sanitizes the whitespace away and hits
its empty early-return.

Not reachable by saving through the UI, since saveList now rejects empty-after-sanitize.
Reachable via hand-edited or corrupted sync storage.

Done: the three gates agree on one definition of empty, applied consistently.

title: Dead assertion and missing dedupe defence from .6
description:
Two one-liners found during oculist-l6m.6 review.

1. test/dim_highlight.test.js:204 asserts priorities.dim === 0, but 0 is the CSS spec default
   for Highlight.priority, so deleting the assignment at content.js:1977 can never fail it.
   The assertion cannot detect what it appears to test.
2. normalizeWorkList (content.js:102-109) does not dedupe terms. updateDimHighlight skips the
   active term BY INDEX, not by text, so a session payload with a repeated term would put the
   active term's own ranges into the dim set. Unreachable through the UI today because
   addChipTerm dedupes on add.

Done: the assertion tests something real or is removed with a comment saying why; normalizeWorkList dedupes.
notes:
THIRD ONE-LINER from the .5 review: the else branch inside the committed-Enter block (content.js:2833-2836) is unreachable, because performListSearch() always sets firstEnter = true when searchRanges.length > 0. Remove it or explain why it stays.
FOURTH ONE-LINER from the .7 review: the Lite Mode toggle rescan (content.js:4232) fires even when the bar is closed and wrap is null, paying a full buildPageIndex() for no visible effect. Guard on wrap.
FIFTH ONE-LINER, from the .19 re-review: content.js:2680-2689 nests if (!hasActiveChip) inside if (!term) where if (!term && !hasActiveChip) reads better. Cosmetic only.
SIXTH ONE-LINER, from the .27 review: .oc-settings-reset-btn's accessible name is the literal string '↺ Reset', so the glyph leaks into what a screen reader announces. Move the glyph out of the accessible name.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: All six one-liners landed and review-passed. Notes: (1) dim priority assertion removed with mutation evidence (0 is the spec default, deletion undetectable); (2) normalizeWorkList dedupes exact-string keep-first with activeIndex remap - known pre-existing divergence: addChipTerm trims before comparing, normalizeWorkList does not, so a crafted payload ['a',' a'] still yields two chips (unreachable via UI); (3) unreachable else independently re-verified and removed; (4) lite-mode rescan guarded on wrap - guard is defensively redundant since __ocDestroy clears workListTerms; (6) reset glyph now aria-hidden - cosmetic risk noted by reviewer: inline-flex may collapse the glyph span's trailing space so the visual gap between the glyph and 'Reset' could shrink; untested, fix with gap/margin if it looks wrong.
